title: Listo Pairing Ledger
lede: Every subclass in the modlist enumerated and scored, then built a second way wherever the first pass had settled into a habit — 265 bodies across ten axes and three acts, paired with every other. Saves and Skills are derived from evidence rather than judged; damage-type overlap, single-source rescue and class contention are charged. Skills now measures the checks that cannot be prepared for — traps, secret doors and routine town dialogue — because every named gate in the run turned out to be buyable with a 100-gold respec or bypassable without a check at all. The entries are the Pareto frontier over the four blocks; the field table is the record.
footer: Built 19-20 August 2026 against the installed Listonomicon 10.2 paks. 157 subclasses enumerated, 170 bodies scored and 95 variants added, 34,980 pairings computed. Skills derived from per-act check modifiers, saves from proficiency sets, and every pairing charged for its holes, its idle bodies, its damage-type overlap and its contention. Two known limitations. Proficiency bonus is pinned at +3/+4/+5 by act; strict rules give +6 for characters 17-20, and rescoring on that convention moves 5 of the top 20 and changes the Act III Skills rung on 87 of 265 chassis, with no pairing moving more than 0.9 points. And Skills rung 5 is unreachable by construction: the best pair in the field averages 0.79 against a 0.75 threshold, but Perception against the 15-25 trap band peaks at 0.60 for anyone in the roster, and the worst-check rule holds the rung down. No two-character party covers this run's detection load — read a 4 as excellent. Every number here is derived at render time.

Ossuary.note: Death has martial weapons but no heavy armour and no Extra Attack, so Fighter opens: heavy armour, shields, a fighting style and Action Surge, at the price of the Cleric's Wis+Cha save pair. Cleric 18 keeps Improved Reaper at 17 and the third Channel Divinity charge, so Control Undead and Turn Undead stop competing. It gives up any real single-target damage — necrotic Divine Strike on one attack is a rounding error under Absolute Wrath.

Archivist.note: The domain's double proficiency in two Int skills is Expertise ×2 on a chassis that already casts Guidance, and CCC's Magical Secrets at 6 and 10 buy the control the 88-spell Cleric list lacks. Fighter first patches the worst hole — light armour on a d8 caster — and adds a third Action. What it never buys is damage: this body is a utility and control chassis with a rung-1 attack all run.

Vigil.note: Life already grants heavy armour, so Cleric stays the level-1 class and keeps Wis+Cha; Fighter 2 is bought purely for Action Surge, Second Wind and a fighting style. Supreme Healing at 17 and the third Channel Divinity charge at 18 are the reason the split stops at two. It contributes nothing to tempo — every turn is a heal, a buff or Spirit Guardians.

Corona.note: Radiance of the Dawn is a repeatable AoE on the short-rest Channel Divinity clock, and the third charge at Cleric 18 is what makes it an engine rather than an opener. Warding Flare fires twice a round on Lone Wolf's spare reaction — disadvantage is scale-invariant, so it is the one Cleric mitigation layer that does not decay. Fighter first buys the heavy armour the domain refuses to grant.

Bramble.note: Nature is the only domain with built-in Shillelagh, so a Wisdom body swings with no feat tax — but it has no Extra Attack, which is exactly what six Fighter levels supply. Level order is Cleric 1 for heavy armour and Wis+Cha, then Fighter to 5 by character 6, then the Cleric block; Divine Strike's cold/fire/lightning choice arrives late but is a real Absolute Wrath hedge. It gives up Master of Nature at 17 and the third CD charge.

Thunderhead.note: The caster Tempest: Destructive Wrath maximising thunder and lightning on three short-rest Channel Divinity charges at Cleric 18, Wrath of the Storm as the repeatable no-concentration rider, Stormborn's flight at 17. Fighter 2 adds only Action Surge and Second Wind because the domain already carries heavy armour and martial weapons. Locked to two damage types, which Absolute Wrath punishes from Act II.

Galvanic.note: The weapon reading of Tempest: Fighter 5's Extra Attack plus Divine Strike's thunder rider and Battle Master manoeuvres make the turns weapon swings, with Destructive Wrath held for the one big Call Lightning or Thunderwave rather than spent every fight. Trades the 17 capstone, the third CD charge and two spell tiers for a real attack routine and a short-rest damage pool.

Mimicry.note: Trickery gives a two-person party almost nothing before Improved Duplicity at 17, so the split is built to make the intervening levels pay: Rogue as the level-1 class buys four skills, Expertise ×2 and Dex+Int saves, and Thief's second bonus action stacks with Lone Wolf's for three decoy moves, hides and item uses a turn. It gives up heavy armour entirely and the third Channel Divinity charge, so Invoke Duplicity stays on two charges.

Clarion.note: The only domain with true Extra Attack (CCC at 6), and War Priest's bonus-action strike sits on top of it — with Lone Wolf that is four weapon swings plus one or two bonus-action strikes, behind heavy armour and martial weapons. Level order is Cleric to 8 first, so Extra Attack, Divine Strike and War Priest are all online by character 8, which is the rubric's literal Act I rung-5 recipe; the rest of the run only adds bigger numbers. Battle Master pays for the third Action and the manoeuvre riders. Gives up Avatar of Battle at 17's replacement — it keeps it — but loses the third CD charge.

Sigil.note: The only domain that hands a Cleric native Counterspell, which in a duo has no wizard to hold it, and Lone Wolf's spare reaction pays for it; Arcane Abjuration's level-threshold banish is slot-free denial off a Channel Divinity charge. Fighter first supplies the armour the domain does not. Arcane Mastery's 6th-to-9th wizard spells at 17 are the reason the Cleric block runs to 18.

Crucible.note: The most durable Cleric in the list, and the split is built to protect that: Cleric 1 for heavy armour and Wis+Cha, Heavy Armour Master out of the Act I feat budget on top of Blessing of the Forge's +1 AC, then Soul of the Forge's second +1 and fire resistance, and Saint of Forge and Fire's non-magical physical resistance at 17. Fighter 2 adds Second Wind and a third Action. Its offence never leaves rung 1 and it spends half its early feat budget on armour.

Lychgate.note: Sentinel at Death's Door turns a critical hit on the partner into a normal hit, Wis-modifier times per long rest, off the reaction Lone Wolf leaves spare — prevention aimed outward, on top of Revivify, Raise Dead, Death Ward and Circle of Mortality's maximised healing at 0 HP. Keeper of Souls at 17 finally adds the no-action outward source the axis wants, which is why Rescue holds in Act III where most domains fall. Fighter first for armour; the body deals essentially no damage.

Decree.note: Every buff or heal aimed at the partner buys them a free weapon attack, at no resource cost, every turn — the single best action-economy domain in a two-player run, and Order's Wrath at 17 keys off an ally hitting, which with one partner is entirely reliable. Order's Demand is AoE charm plus disarm off a short-rest Channel Divinity charge with no concentration attached. Heavy armour comes from the domain, so Fighter 2 is bought only for Action Surge. Own damage stays at rung 1 all run.

Concord.note: With exactly two characters Emboldening Bond is permanently online — a no-action d4 on every attack, check and save for both bodies — and it sits on top of Sanctuary, Aid, Beacon of Hope, Greater Restoration and Death Ward, which is prevention, restoration and a no-action outward source at once. Peace grants the weakest armour of the strong domains, so Fighter opens for heavy armour and Action Surge at the cost of the Wis+Cha pair.

Gloaming.note: Twilight Sanctuary is the rubric's own Act I rung-5 rescue anchor — 1d6 plus Cleric level temporary HP to everything ending its turn inside, or a charm and fright cleanse, for a Channel Divinity charge a short rest refunds, costing no concentration. The third charge at 18 and Twilight Shroud's half cover at 17 are why the Cleric block runs deep; Fighter 2 buys only Action Surge on top of the domain's heavy armour and martial weapons.

Nightwatch.note: The Twilight domain read as a weapon body: Fighter 5's Extra Attack turns the domain's martial weapons into an actual attack routine and Battle Master manoeuvres carry riders, while Twilight Sanctuary keeps running as a no-concentration aura underneath. It gives up Twilight Shroud, the third Channel Divinity charge and two spell tiers, so the sanctuary runs on two charges and the spell list stops at 7th.

Sinew.note: The only Cleric domain with Haste on its own list, which is the strongest action-economy spell a two-person party can cast — but the domain grants no martial weapons and no Extra Attack, so Fighter supplies both. Avatar of Battle's transform carries non-magical physical resistance from Cleric 6 and a second charge at 10. Haste holds this body's one concentration slot, so both control axes and AoE are scored without Spirit Guardians; that is the trade the build makes.

Immolate.note: Heavy armour, martial weapons and Priest of Zeal's bonus-action strike from level 1, and Fighter 5 adds the Extra Attack the domain never gets — attack, attack, bonus-action strike, with Action Surge for a third Action. Consuming Fervor stays as the burst: maximised fire or thunder, twice per short rest from Cleric 6. Nothing here holds concentration, which is rare on a Wisdom caster and is this body's quiet advantage in a pair with only two slots. It gives up Blaze of Glory and the third CD charge.

Conflagrant.note: The caster reading of Zeal: the turns are Fireball, Flame Strike and Destructive Wave rather than swings, with Consuming Fervor maximising them on three short-rest Channel Divinity charges at Cleric 18 and Haste held on the partner. Heavy armour keeps it in the pack; Fighter 2 supplies only Action Surge and Second Wind. The whole AoE plan is fire, which Absolute Wrath's layered resistances punish from Act II.

Witchbane.note: The anti-caster martial: Witch Hunter's Strike is a force rider that doubles against anything concentrating, and force is the least-resisted type in the list, while Spell Shield puts temp HP, spell-damage resistance and advantage on spell saves onto the partner for a short-rest Channel Divinity charge. Fighter 5 supplies the Extra Attack the domain lacks and Battle Master dice on the short-rest clock. It gives up Spell Shield's five-target upgrade at 17 and the third CD charge.

Doomsayer.note: Eldritch Contagion is single-target control that costs no concentration and fires as a bonus action off any level 1+ spell cast, and Prophecy of Doom spreads the same effect table over a 5m sphere at 27m for one short-rest Channel Divinity charge — action-economy denial that never competes with the partner's slot. The third charge at 18 and the 10d10 psychic upgrade at 17 are the reason the Cleric block runs deep. Fighter opens for the armour the domain refuses.

Penumbra.note: Invocation of Night Blinds every enemy in 9m that fails a Constitution save for rounds equal to Cleric level, off a short-rest Channel Divinity charge with no concentration — slot-free repeatable area control, which is the top rung's literal definition, and the third charge at 18 makes it three times a short rest. Ward of Shadows fires twice a round on Lone Wolf's second reaction. Fighter opens for heavy armour; the domain gives none and the body has no offence of its own.

Reverie.note: Deep Slumber is area control at spell level 1 that leaves Torpor behind — quarter movement, no reactions, and only one of attack, action or bonus action — and Inception gives every Int- or Wis-save spell disadvantage on the target's first save, which the rubric prices above a raw DC and which does not decay across the run. Fighter opens for armour. The domain adds no damage at all beyond Potent Spellcasting on Mind Sliver.

Wellspring.note: Natural Recovery is the only in-day slot refund in the class and it moves the axis Lone Wolf makes worst; otherwise this is the bare Druid chassis — a 117-spell prepared list, a maintained summon set that costs no concentration under 13458, and no body of its own. Fighter opens for heavy armour and shields on a d8 caster plus a third Action, trading the Int+Wis save pair for Str+Con.

Therian.split: Druid 17 (Circle of the Moon) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Therian.note: Combat Wild Shape is a second full HP bar on a bonus action twice per short rest, with Lunar Mend on top, and under the Wild Shape Overhaul multiclass features keep working inside the form — Action Surge explicitly among them, which is why Fighter is the dip rather than an armour class whose proficiency the beast form would waste. CR 3 forms with Wild Shape Extra Attack put the multiattack no other circle has on the body. Beast statlines are flat, so the whole plan is outrun by Act III.

Moonveil.note: The casting Moon: the turns are spells and a maintained summon set, with Combat Wild Shape held as a bonus-action second HP bar for the round the plan goes wrong rather than as the plan itself. Fighter opens for heavy armour and shields, which a body that spends most of its turns in its own skin actually gets to use, plus Action Surge. It gives up the CR 3 attack routine entirely.

Mycelia.split: Druid 17 (Circle of the Spores) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Mycelia.note: The only Druid circle with a real Extra Attack (4018), and it stacks with Shillelagh, Symbiotic Entity's +1d6 and 68 temp HP at Druid 17, and Spreading Spores as an at-will area tick under a Cloudkill burst; Fungal Infestation adds four maintained bodies per long rest on top of the class summon suite. Fighter 3 buys Action Surge, a fighting style and short-rest superiority dice without costing Druid level, which every temp-HP number here keys off. It stays in medium armour.

Zodiac.note: Star Druid Tweaks moves Cosmic Omens onto the short rest, so Weal is a dozen swings of +1d6 on the partner's saving throws per rest cycle — repeatable no-concentration prevention — and Woe is the same subtraction aimed at an enemy's. Chalice doubles every outward heal, which is what the Life domain dip is for: heavy armour and shields on a d8 caster, plus Disciple of Life and Preserve Life on the same Wisdom stat. Dragon form floors concentration saves at 10.

Tidewrack.note: Wrath of the Sea is a bonus-action Wisdom-scaled damage-and-push every turn that spends no concentration and runs off a Wild Shape charge, sitting under Evard's Black Tentacles and Sleet Storm — the two spells the rubric names at the top of the area-control ladder. The Tempest dip is the coherent one: heavy armour, martial weapons and Destructive Wrath maximising the circle's own Lightning Bolt, Thunderwave and Gust of Wind. Stormborn's flight and triple elemental resistance land at Druid 10.

Fulminant.note: The level 10 clause makes Lightning, Thunder and Cold ignore Resistance and treat Immunity as Resistance — one of the very few resistance strips in the list, and what lets an elemental blaster keep scaling under Absolute Wrath — while Storm Shift buys 51 temp HP until long rest for one Wild Shape charge. Tempest is the dip that compounds it: heavy armour, and Destructive Wrath maximising exactly the damage types the strip protects. Its single-target damage never leaves rung 2.

Hoarfrost.note: The level 10 clause prones every creature that fails a save against a Cold Druid spell, and Ice Storm, Cone of Cold and Snilloc's are not concentration — area hard control riding damage that was being cast anyway, at no cost to the pair's two slots. Winter Spirit adds Wisdom as bonus Cold to every damage spell and +1d6 on melee hits off one charge, with 85 temp HP behind it at Druid 17; Nature is the dip because it grants heavy armour and Shillelagh, which is the melee rider's intended pairing. Locked to Cold with no strip before the level 14 immunity.

Dreamwarden.note: Scored as the bare Druid chassis plus the dip, because the Book of Druids pack's levels 2, 6 and 10 features are recorded as unverified and the class file explicitly forbids assuming they match the same author's standalone Circle of Dreams. The Life dip is chosen on the presumed identity — heavy armour, shields, Disciple of Life and Preserve Life on the same Wisdom stat — and is what the scores below actually rest on outside the class chassis.

Beastcall.note: The largest maintained body count the act allows — Conjure Animals and Summon Beast last until long rest and cost no concentration under 13458, Flock of Familiars and Find Familiar stack on top, and Mighty Summoner makes all of them ignore physical resistance — with every Spirit Totem an aura aimed at the other body: Bear's temp HP, Flumph turning every heal into two. Life is the dip that Flumph doubles, and it supplies the heavy armour a summoner standing behind its own wall still wants. The body itself never attacks.

Pyrewake.note: A permanent extra body that also casts your spells from its own position — a second point of origin for AoE, which a two-body party cannot otherwise generate — on top of the class summon suite. Warden of Life at 7 plus Revivify at 5 and Mass Cure Wounds at 9 is prevention and restoration in one list, and the Life dip stacks Disciple of Life and heavy armour onto it. Its own damage stays at rung 1 and the AoE is all fire.

Cataclysm.note: Four aspects spanning fire/radiant, lightning/thunder, cold/piercing and force/bludgeoning is the broadest damage-type coverage in the circle set and the direct answer to Absolute Wrath's layered resistances, with Revelations as short-rest bursts under scaling cantrips that need no summon and no gear. Tempest is the dip that maximises the Stormstrike half and supplies heavy armour. Only two aspects are held before Druid 10, so the spread is really three at the Act II judging point.

Seelie.note: Fey Presence is area charm-or-fear off a short-rest charge with no concentration — the rung-4 clause — and Dominate Person at patron 9 lands on a short-rest pact slot rather than a long-rest one, so the control clock is the best in the patron set. Fighter opens because light armour with no shield is the patron's floor and Action Surge on an Eldritch Blast body is four more beams; the cost is the Wisdom and Charisma save pair, replaced by Strength and Constitution. Nothing here is aimed at the partner.

Brimstone.note: The only patron whose expanded list gives a real burst under Eldritch Cone — Fireball, Wall of Fire, Flame Strike — and the Zeal dip is the one that compounds it: Consuming Fervor maximises fire on a Channel Divinity charge a short rest refunds, and the domain hands a light-armour caster heavy armour, shields and martial weapons at level 1 while Cleric keeps the Wisdom and Charisma saves. Fiendish Resilience at patron 10 is a proportional resistance re-picked every rest. The whole burst half is fire, which Absolute Wrath punishes hardest.

Hollowmind.split: Warlock 17 (The Great Old One) / Mesmerist 3 (Aspect of the Eyebiter)
Hollowmind.note: Evard's Black Tentacles at patron 7 comes off a short-rest pact slot, which is top-of-ladder area control on a repeatable clock, and Mortal Reminder's area fear fires far more often than its text suggests because several Eldritch Blast beams a round make several crit checks. The Mesmerist dip is bought for control, not armour: Hypnotic Stare is a permanent bonus-action penalty to one enemy's saves costing no resource and no concentration, Sundering pushes that penalty onto its AC, and Towering Ego adds Charisma to this body's own Wisdom saves. It stays in light armour with no shield, which is the price.

Malefic.note: The one patron that turns the chassis melee at level 1, and Paladin is the dip that costs it nothing: heavy armour, shields and the same Wisdom and Charisma saves the Warlock would have granted, plus Divine Smite converting short-rest pact slots into burst on top of Eldritch Smite, and Vow of Enmity for single-target advantage. Thirsting Blade's Extra Attack, Hexblade's Curse's crit range and Accursed Spectre's maintained third body do the rest. Nothing in the plan holds concentration, which is unusual for a Charisma caster and is the patron's quiet advantage in a pair holding only two slots.

Vowbearer.note: A Hexblade melee shell bought on a Paladin clock: six Paladin levels trade Mystic Arcanum's 8th and 9th tiers for Aura of Protection, which adds a Charisma modifier of six to both bodies' saving throws at Listo's 9m radius — the single largest defensive purchase a Charisma pair can make, and one that only one of the two should ever buy. Master of Hexes at Warlock 14 still lands, so the curse still spreads. What it gives up is the top of the Warlock spell table entirely.

Empyrean.note: The only Warlock with outward rescue, and it is the good kind: Healing Light is a bonus-action heal spending no slot, so Lone Wolf's second bonus action buys two a turn alongside a full Action, and Revivify at patron 5 plus Greater Restoration at 9 both ride the short-rest pact clock. Free Sacred Flame is the save-based radiant answer to the high-AC targets Eldritch Blast's attack roll misses. Cleric 3 (Life) is the dip that fixes the armour — heavy plus shields on a d8 body — and adds Preserve Life on a short-rest charge. There is still no Death Ward and no Sanctuary, so no true prevention.

Aetherburn.note: Warp turns every Eldritch Blast beam into a Force detonation in a 3m radius, which is a genuinely repeatable at-will area engine in the least-resisted damage type — and Perils of the Warp pays for it in maximum hit points every turn, which is the one resource a duo cannot spare. Twilight is the dip chosen against exactly that: heavy armour, martial weapons, and Twilight Sanctuary putting temporary HP on both bodies every round off a short-rest Channel Divinity charge with no concentration. Gellar's Field at patron 10 finally negates the drain once per short rest.

Riposte.note: The mono Battle Master's whole problem is that it rolls a 0 on skills; Bard 3 taken at characters 6–8 buys Expertise ×2, three extra Lore proficiencies, Cutting Words on Lone Wolf's spare reaction and Song of Rest, and costs only Improved Combat Superiority (18) and the fourth attack (20). Everything the chassis does still runs off the short-rest superiority pool.

Nineteen.note: The one Fighter where the last three levels genuinely beat a dip: Superior Critical (15) widens the range to 18–20, Survivor (18) regenerates below half, and Expansion's fourth attack at 20 makes eight swings a round under Lone Wolf, all at a 15% crit rate with Heroic Warrior rerolling the misses. It pays for that with nothing at all on control, rescue or skills.

Battlemage.note: The weapon Eldritch Knight: Str swings first, Int is a support stat funding Shield, Mirror Image, Misty Step and one concentration buff. Mono is justified by Expansion's own table — Arcane Charge at 15, the second Improved War Magic at 18 and any Wizard spell at 20 — but its 3rd–4th tier ceiling means both control axes are background by Act III.

Sculptor.note: The Intelligence build of the Eldritch Knight rather than the weapon one: a single stat drives attack conversion, spell DCs and the Wizard slots, so Improved War Magic at 12 spends two of three attacks on a real Fireball instead of a 2nd-tier one. Sculpt Spells is what makes area damage safe in a two-body party. Level order is Fighter 1–12, Wizard 1–6, Fighter 13–14.

Arrowfall.note: Arcane Shots are repeatable single-target hard control that spends no concentration, which is the rung-4 clause; the Ranger 3 taken at characters 6–8 bolts on a Companion's Bond beast that acts every round and can Help a downed partner up as a bonus action, filling the two axes the mono Archer reads zero on. Costs Ever-Ready Shot and Arcane Shot Improved.

Sledge.split: Fighter 17 (Brute) / Blood Hunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer)
Sledge.note: Two resource-free per-hit dice on every one of six attacks: Brute Force scaling 1d4/1d6/1d8 and a Crimson Rite on the same swing, with Rite of the Dawn putting one of them on Radiant against Absolute Wrath's layered resistances. Ghostslayer 3 also hands over four short-rest Blood Maledicts, which is the only debuff this chassis will ever own. Brutish Durability lands at character 7 and never leaves.

Palisade.note: The dedicated protector, with the rubric's own named Act I rung-4 rescue bolted on for two levels: Twilight Sanctuary taken at characters 6–7 temp-HPs both bodies every round for one short-rest Channel Divinity charge, on top of Warding Maneuver's ranged damage prevention and Unwavering Mark pulling attention onto the armoured half. Vigilant Defender at 18 is why it does not dip further.

Kinesis.note: Artificer 2 at characters 6–7 is the cheapest thing an Intelligence Fighter can buy: Sleight of Hand for the Act II Araj gate, Enhanced Weapon and Enhanced Defense as permanent stat a gold-starved pair will never find, and a Homunculus body — all off the stat the psionic dice already scale on. Protective Field is the rescue; the psionic pool is the reason it stops at 18 rather than 20.

Graven.note: Rune DCs key off Constitution, so Lone Wolf's +4 goes to Con and Wis and Dexterity is bought back with Resilient. Knowledge 2 at characters 6–7 adds Guidance at will and doubled proficiency in two knowledge skills, which with Rune Knight's own Sleight of Hand is the only Fighter in the list holding a plausible answer to all three acts' skill gates. Master of Runes at 15 puts the whole toolbox on the short-rest clock twice over.

Ronin.note: Fighting Spirit is three advantages per rest; Reckless Attack is advantage on every turn forever, so Barbarian 2 at characters 6–7 frees the bonus action Samurai would otherwise spend and adds Danger Sense on top. Elegant Courtier at character 9 buys a fifth saving-throw proficiency, which nothing else in the class can do. Contributes nothing to control, rescue or crowds.

Ambuscade.note: A deliberately front-loaded alpha strike: Steady Aim's scaling rider and Extra Attack by character 5, Assassin's restored Action and guaranteed crits on the surprised by 8, Dread Ambusher's initiative and first-round extra attack by 11. Improved Extra Attack only arrives at character 17, so the middle of the run is where this body is weakest relative to the act, and surprise stops being available long before the run ends.

Twinshade.note: Legion of One is never implemented, so Fighter 16–20 buys the Echo Knight nothing and the last five levels go elsewhere. Thief at characters 6–8 gives a third bonus action for manifesting and swapping the echo, and Grave 2 at 15–16 adds Circle of Mortality's maximised healing on a downed body plus Path to the Grave timed onto the partner's biggest swing. Unleash Incarnation fires once per Attack action, so both Lone Wolf Actions and Action Surge each generate an extra swing.

Amethyst.note: A permanent third combatant that shares your initiative and needs no bonus action to command, plus Rallying Surge turning one Action Surge into reaction attacks for the partner and the dragon at once. Order 2 at characters 6–7 stacks Voice of Authority on top: every heal you put on the partner buys them a free weapon attack, which is the same currency the whole chassis trades in. Stops at 18 for Enduring Commander's resistances.

Hourfall.note: Borrowed Time literally hands the other body an Action, and Borrowed Time and Action Surge cannot be used on the same turn — which is the argument for mono: the second Action Surge charge at 17, Chronobreak at 18 and the fourth attack at 20 are what make alternating turns worth more than any three levels bought elsewhere. Rewind is a short-rest 'the partner does not fail that save'.

Undertow.split: Rogue 3 (Thief) / Monk 17 (Way of the Open Hand)
Undertow.note: Rogue first because the level-1 node is the only place four skill proficiencies and Expertise ×2 exist, and a Monk otherwise reads zero out of combat; Thief's third bonus action on top of Lone Wolf's two means three Flurries a round, which is three more chances at Stunning Strike and three more free Topple/Push riders. The cost is Diamond Soul slipping to character 17.

Umbra.note: Shadow Arts already buys Hide, Pass Without Trace and Darkness out of the ki pool, so Assassin is the subclass that converts that stealth into damage — restored Action at the start of combat and guaranteed crits on the surprised. It is deliberately front-loaded: by Act III fights start in the open, the 2d6 Sneak Attack is flat, and only Stunning Strike is still doing act-relative work.

Quintessence.split: Monk 17 (Way of the Four Elements) / Druid 3 (Circle of the Land)
Quintessence.note: The disciplines are the only repeatable AoE a Monk owns, and the cost is that one ki pool funds the disciplines, the Flurries and Stunning Strike at once. Druid 3 at characters 6–8 is the cheapest relief available: real spell slots off Wisdom, Natural Recovery as the class's only in-day refund, Guidance, and a Find Familiar body — none of it needing a second stat.

Wyrmcall.split: Monk 17 (Way of the Ascendant Dragon) / Cleric 3 (Tempest Domain)
Wyrmcall.note: Draconic Strike is a toggle, so set the whole subclass to lightning and Tempest's Destructive Wrath maximises the Breath of the Dragon it is already firing every round for no bonus action. Tempest 3 at characters 6–8 also brings Wrath of the Storm, Wisdom slots and a second lightning source, on the stat the Ki Save DC already uses. Aspect of the Wyrm at character 14 is the only Monk feature that buffs the partner.

Starhand.split: Monk 17 (Way of the Astral Self) / Inquisitor 3 (Vengeance Inquisition)
Starhand.note: The single-stat Monk paired with the single-stat half-martial: the astral arms attack and damage on Wisdom, Unarmoured Defence and the Ki Save DC are Wisdom, and Vengeance's Monster Tactician is Expertise plus double Wisdom modifier on an Intelligence skill — a real skill total on a body with no Intelligence at all. Damage lands as Force, the least-resisted type in the run.

Whetstone.note: Kensei is the Monk that can carry an attuned Legendary weapon, and Listo's weapon pool is enormous where its unarmed pool is not; Swashbuckler is the Rogue that lands Sneak Attack on it without needing advantage or a second melee body, which a duo often cannot supply. Agile Parry's +2 AC is free on nearly every turn. Sneak Attack stays at 2d6 forever, which is why single-target slides in Act III.

Deathless.note: The one Monk where the last six levels beat any dip, because all of them are the same feature: Mastery of Death at 11 spends 1 ki and no action to refuse a knockout, Touch of the Long Death at 17 is a 1–10 ki nuke, Empty Body at 18 adds invisibility and resistance to everything but force, and Perfect Self at 20 refills the pool the whole stack runs on. Losing either body ends the fight, and this is the body that will not be lost.

Physick.note: Mercy's named gap is prevention: it heals and cures but nothing stops the damage arriving. Twilight 3 at characters 6–8 patches exactly that — a no-action temp-HP aura on both bodies for one short-rest Channel Divinity charge, plus a charm and fright cleanse — while Flurry of Healing and Harm at character 14 makes the healing itself free on the attack routine. Hand of Ultimate Mercy at 17 is a long-rest in-combat resurrection.

Solstice.split: Monk 17 (Way of the Sun Soul) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Solstice.note: The only Way that makes a Monk a real ranged character, and the odd one out because it scales on Dexterity — so the Ki Save DC is soft and Stunning Strike lands less often than on any other Monk here. Fighter 3 at characters 7–9 buys Action Surge, which on this chassis is a whole second round of Sun Bolts and a second Searing Arc Strike, plus superiority dice whose DC keys off the Dexterity it already maxes.

Squall.split: Monk 17 (Warrior of the Elements) / Barbarian 3 (Path of Ginnungagap)
Squall.note: Elemental Strikes replace the default unarmed attack, so opportunity attacks carry the extended range, the chosen element and the push/pull rider — control landing on the enemy's turn for free, which is the cheapest economy a duo can buy. Barbarian 3 at characters 6–8 works because a Monk wears no armour: Rage's physical resistance, Danger Sense, and Ginnungagap's advantage on saves against spells arrive nine levels before Diamond Soul does.

Cloister.split: Monk 14 (Way of the Friar) / Cleric 6 (Peace Domain)
Cloister.note: Friar's Bond covers the whole party at Monk 3 in a duo, so Shared Resolve at 11 and Community at 17 are dead weight and the subclass stops paying after Cleansing Wave at 9 — which is the argument for six Cleric levels instead. Peace stacks Emboldening Bond's permanent d4 on both bodies over Friar's own blessing, adds Revivify, Balm of Peace and a second short-rest Channel Divinity charge, and Guardian of Light is the one Monk that keeps Unarmoured Defence behind a shield. It spends one of the pair's two concentration slots to do any of it.

Dawnrite.split: Blood Hunter 18 (Order of the Ghostslayer) / Fighter 2 (none)
Dawnrite.note: Rite Revival at 18 is a literal answer to the run's failure mode — with a Rite active, dropping to 0 restores 1 HP instead — so this Order goes deep and buys only Action Surge and Second Wind at characters 6–7. Brand of Sundering rolls the Crimson Rite die twice, and the Rite is a scaling hemocraft die rather than a flat one, so the rider holds its rung where a 1d6 would not. Nothing here is aimed at the partner.

Moonrend.split: Blood Hunter 17 (Order of the Lycan) / Rogue 3 (Thief)
Moonrend.note: Predatory Strikes already grant a bonus-action unarmed strike that scales off Dexterity and can carry a Crimson Rite; Thief at characters 6–8 adds a third bonus action on top of Lone Wolf's two, so the transformed body throws three of them a round. Resilient Hide's non-magical physical resistance is proportional and does not decay. It gives up the level-18 unlimited transformations and Blood Curse of the Howl.

Alembic.split: Blood Hunter 17 (Order of the Mutant) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Alembic.note: Celerity is +4 to a raw Dexterity score against a modlist that removed the ability cap, Cruelty is an extra attack after any attack, and both come off a short-rest Mutagen charge. Battle Master at characters 6–8 fills the two axes the Order reads nearest zero on — its manoeuvre DC keys off the Dexterity the mutagens are already inflating — and adds Action Surge. It trades away Expert Mutagencraft's +5 at 18.

Hemomancer.split: Blood Hunter 14 (Order of the Profane Soul) / Wizard 6 (School of Evocation)
Hemomancer.note: The Intelligence Profane Soul: pact slots, Wizard slots, Brand DCs and Dark Augmentation's save bonus all key off one stat, so the six Wizard levels cost nothing in spread. Sculpt Spells is what makes a Fireball castable in a two-body party at all. Brand of the Sapping Scar at character 11 stays the point of the Order — blanket Disadvantage on the branded creature's saves, no concentration, so it never competes with the Wizard spell this body is already holding.

Scarbrand.split: Blood Hunter 18 (Order of the Profane Soul) / Fighter 2 (none)
Scarbrand.note: The Profane Soul read as a martial rather than as a caster: Dexterity carries the weapon, Intelligence only has to be high enough for the Brand DC, and Mystic Frenzy turns the pact cantrip into a bonus-action weapon attack every round. Hexblade's curse adds the proficiency bonus to the next damage roll. Action Surge at characters 6–7 is the only thing bought outside the class, and Blood Curse of the Soul Eater at 18 is why it goes that deep.

Wrothgar.note: Fighter 1 buys the Str+Con saves, heavy armour and a fighting style the Barbarian table cannot, Fighter 2 buys Action Surge, and Barbarian 18 still reaches Retaliation at 14 and Indomitable Might. It gives up Primal Champion and has no answer to a crowd beyond cleave.

Colossus.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Giant) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Colossus.note: The melee reading of the Giant: Barbarian 1 first for Str+Con saves and Unarmoured Defence, Barbarian 14 for Demiurgic Colossus's Huge toggle and +10 ft reach, with a late Battle Master block for Action Surge and manoeuvre riders. It reaches its shape at 14 and spends the run before that as an ordinary Extra Attack body.

Trebuchet.split: Fighter 3 (Battle Master) / Barbarian 17 (Path of the Giant)
Trebuchet.note: The thrower. Fighter 1 supplies Thrown Weapon Fighting, heavy armour and the Str+Con saves; Goon's fixes put Reckless Attack and Brutal Critical on thrown attacks and scale Rage's throw bonus to +8 for Giant at 16. It buys reach and a resistance-proof second damage type at the cost of ever having a bonus-action attack.

Fluxroot.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of Wild Magic) / Blood Hunter 3 (Order of the Ghostslayer)
Fluxroot.note: Blood Hunter is taken at characters 2-4 so Crimson Rite and Rite of the Dawn are online before the subclass is, giving a permanent Radiant rider, Necrotic resistance and four short-rest Blood Curses on a chassis whose own kit is random. Magic Awareness with Goon's fix is a pair-wide anti-caster save bonus; Bolstering Magic hands the partner a slot and lands on no axis this schema carries.

Ursine.note: The one Barbarian whose whole kit is Rage-gated, so Primal Champion at 20 — +4 Str and Con past the 20 ceiling to a cap of 24, and a Rage charge back every turn — is worth more here than three levels anywhere else: Bear Heart's near-blanket resistance and Bestial Attunement's taunt stop being a per-day budget. Heavy armour is refused outright because Goon's disables Bear resistance in it.

Forebear.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Ancestral Guardian) / Paragon 3 (Prodigy)
Forebear.note: The only outward-facing Barbarian: Ancestral Protectors is a free no-concentration taunt-with-teeth from character 3, and Spirit Shield is a reaction that eats damage aimed at the partner, which Lone Wolf's second reaction lets you spend twice. Prodigy's Sheer Will adds temp HP and flat reduction; the Paragon block is slotted at characters 4-6 so it is live for the whole run.

Spikework.note: Thief's second bonus action is the only thing that fixes this subclass's stated flaw — the armour-spike attack competing with Rage for the one bonus action — so the spike actually lands every turn on top of Extra Attack. It is still a 1d4 that stops mattering, and the medium-metal-armour lock forfeits Unarmoured Defence for nothing.

Clawlord.note: Claws add an attack to every Attack action, so two Lone Wolf Actions plus Action Surge is nine swings with Rage's rider on each — the highest attack count in the Barbarian file, online at character 7. Claws forbid a shield, which is exactly why Fighter 1 is taken for heavy armour, and Infectious Fury's reaction-theft is genuine no-concentration turn removal from 12.

Moraine.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Juggernaut) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Moraine.note: Resolute Stance is at-will Disadvantage on every attack against you and is scale-invariant, so it does not decay; Thunderous Blows plus Hurricane Strike is a push-and-prone routine that costs no concentration and hands the partner a free reaction attack. The Battle Master block at characters 4-6 adds Trip Attack, which stacks with the push rather than duplicating it.

Tundrine.split: Fighter 2 (none) / Barbarian 18 (Path of the Storm Herald)
Tundrine.note: Tundra Storm Aura streams temp HP at the partner every single turn for no rest resource, and Shielding Storm at 10 hands them a proportional elemental resistance outright — the only sustained outward mitigation in the class. Fighter 1's heavy armour keeps the body that has to stand in its own 10 ft aura alive; its own aura damage is far under par at every point.

Zealbrand.split: Fighter 3 (Battle Master) / Barbarian 17 (Path of the Zealot)
Zealbrand.note: Divine Fury scales with Barbarian level rather than sitting flat, so the rider holds its rung all the way to +1d6+8, and it arrives as Radiant or Necrotic against Absolute Wrath's layered physical resistances. Fanatical Focus is a save reroll every Rage, and Rage Beyond Death at character 17 makes the body unkillable inside a Rage; Warrior of the Gods scores on durability, not rescue.

Nullwarden.note: The dedicated anti-caster in a modlist whose own balance docs call ordinary enemies wild magic sorcerers and warlocks: Magic Syphoning is a counterspell on a reaction, Spell Eater turns enemy magic into sustain at no rest cost, and Null Warrior's spell-save advantage plus crit downgrade patches the Barbarian's worst hole. Fighter 2 supplies heavy armour and the third Action the class never gets.

Voltaic.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Lightning Vessel) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Voltaic.note: The only Constitution-primary Barbarian: Vessel DCs, Electrified Chains' +2x Con rider and Fulgurant Strike's interrupt burst all key off the same stat that already drives HP and Unarmoured Defence. The bonus-action bottleneck the class file warns about breaks at Barbarian 10, where the free Lightning Step lands and +Con to Dexterity checks quietly answers the Act II pickpocket gate.

Gravewalk.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Revenant) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Gravewalk.note: Flat DR 2 under physical resistance under Lone Wolf's halving, in heavy armour Ghost Armor grants at Barbarian 3, is the tankiest configuration in the file against weapon damage — and Heavy Armour Master on top makes Act I's ceiling. Haunt is a bonus-action no-concentration Frighten that mirrors your damage onto its target and retargets free on a kill.

Panthera.note: Expansion moves Companion's Bond to level 3 and adds the Panther, which uses your proficiency bonus, is proficient in all saving throws, takes your ASIs and can Help as a bonus action — a permanent third body on a short-rest re-summon, joined by the Conjure Animals set from class 9. Its own damage line never rises above par.

Umbrant.note: The archetypal front-loaded body: Dread Ambusher's +3 initiative and first-round extra attack with +1d8 is worth most at character 3 and least at 20, and Stalker's Flurry's free re-attack on a miss keeps pace rather than climbing. Iron Mind at class 7 buys Wisdom and Intelligence save proficiency without spending Resilient, and Shadowy Dodge turns Lone Wolf's spare reaction into the mitigation medium armour never gave it.

Predawn.note: The alpha-strike reading: Dread Ambusher's +3 initiative stacked on Assassin's restored Action and guaranteed crits against the surprised, with Extra Attack taken from Ranger 5 at character 5 and Action Surge arriving at 10. A different resource clock from the deep Gloom Stalker — Sneak Attack is at-will, so nothing here is rationed — but it forfeits Shadowy Dodge, Greater Invisibility and Iron Mind until character 15.

Mothwing.note: Gathered Swarm fires once per round after any attack with no resource and no concentration, and the Flurry of Moths option applies Blind — a repeatable free single-target lockdown — while the teleport option answers being focused when there is no third body to peel. Swashbuckler is taken at characters 4-6 so Sneak Attack lands without needing advantage or an adjacent ally, which is the duo's usual problem.

Wyrmling.note: The drake is a permanent third body whose Infused Strikes adds 1d6 of its essence type whenever any creature within 30 ft lands a weapon attack, so it buffs the partner as well, and Reflexive Resistance is a second life-saving reaction Lone Wolf makes affordable. Almost everything it owns — the re-summon, Drake's Breath, Reflexive Resistance — sits on the long-rest clock, which is why duration reads low.

Thornwit.note: Otherworldly Glamour adds the Wisdom modifier to every Charisma check, and a Lore block at characters 4-6 stacks Expertise x2, three extra proficiencies and Jack of All Trades on top of it — which is how one body clears Hag's Hair on Deception and Araj on Sleight of Hand. It does not reach the Mirror: Otherworldly Glamour adds Wisdom to Charisma checks only, and Religion is Intelligence and dumped, so it ends at bare proficiency against DC 25. Counterspell arrives at class 9 and Fey Reinforcements is a free Summon Fey from 11.

Riftstep.note: Planar Warrior converts all of an attack's damage to Force and adds 2d8 from 11, which deletes Absolute Wrath's layered resistances outright, and it costs a bonus action rather than concentration — so Haste at class 9 is free to sit in the concentration slot and go on the partner. Distant Strike is a real third attack whenever three enemies are present, which in this modlist is most fights.

Quarryman.note: The only conclave whose damage rider costs no concentration, so Slayer's Prey stacks with Hunter's Mark, and Magic-User's Nemesis is a slot-free counterspell-equivalent on a short-rest clock. Nighthawk's Searing Blade strips all resistances for three turns on a failed Con save, which does for the partner's damage type what Hunter's Sense only does for one of your own hits.

Rootward.note: The only Ranger that is a tank: guardian form gives temp HP equal to half Ranger level every turn and +2 max HP per Ranger level from 7, at no action and no resource, and Guardian Aura at 15 heals a hurt partner half your Ranger level every turn with no action either. The price is a movement speed of 5 ft, which is why this is a bow build and why reach is static.

Valkyr.split: Ranger 17 (Conclave of the Dawnstriders) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Valkyr.note: The highest raw damage ceiling of the eleven conclaves: Extra Attack plus Valkyrie's landing attack, Zeal's extra attack every seven swings, and Divine Flurry's five extra attacks at a reduced crit threshold off a 3rd-level slot — with Herald of the Sun converting weapon damage to Radiant or Fire to dodge physical resistance. Valkyrie also imposes Disadvantage on attacks against you when you land close, which is the only mitigation the chassis owns.

Marionette.split: Mesmerist 17 (Aspect of the Trickster) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One)
Marionette.note: Hypnotic Bonds refresh on a short rest and tricks implanted on the partner fire as free actions when their trigger hits, so this body delivers prevention (Mesmeric Mirror auto-misses the triggering attack, Gift of Will adds Cha mod + half level to their Wisdom save, Astounding Avoidance grants Evasion), restoration (Touch Treatment Minor and Major) and outward temp HP without ever spending a turn — and Compel Alacrity hands them Haste. Warlock at characters 4-6 buys Agonizing Blast so it has any damage floor at all.

Basilisk.note: Mono-20 for one named feature no three levels elsewhere touch: at Mesmerist 20 the Resistance boon becomes immunity to all damage while Staring, and Manifold Stare becomes 2d12 with unlimited uses per turn — with True Seeing at 17 and a fourth Masterful Gaze at 19 behind it. Hypnotic Stare is at-will, permanent on one target, bonus action, no resource and no concentration, so nothing here runs on a clock; it has no action surplus and almost no crowd answer.

Witheye.note: The gish reading of Eyebiter lockdown: Spellblade's Scholar's Armament puts Charisma on a main-hand weapon's attack and damage, so the stat that already drives the Stare's save penalty also drives the swing that Painful Stare rides on. Three levels out of Mesmerist trade the level-20 damage-immunity clause and True Seeing's ceiling for a real weapon routine and Arcana expertise from character 6.

Bravado.note: Champion is taken at characters 4-6 for one reason: Improved Critical drops the crit threshold to 19, and a crit with a one-handed piercing weapon is the only in-combat way Panache comes back — which is the resource gating Extra Attack at 5 and Evasion, Uncanny Dodge and a third reaction at 9. Superior Defense adds Charisma to AC while unarmoured, so the primary stat pays twice, and Tier-3 Feints are once-per-short-rest hard control.

Corsair.note: The same rapier, a different clock: Swashbuckler at characters 4-6 gives Sneak Attack with no advantage and no adjacent ally needed, so the damage floor is at-will and does not depend on Panache surviving the day. Cunning Action supplies the mobility the Daredevil's stances want; it gives up Improved Critical, which means Panache genuinely is a long-rest resource here.

Wardstone.note: One Cleric level buys heavy armour, a shield and Wis/Cha saves, and the Arcane Ward then sits on top of AC rather than instead of it — a short-rest absorption pool that Projected Ward spends out of the spare Lone Wolf reaction onto the partner. Gives up Signature Spells and every point of at-will damage.

Nocturne.note: The Bladesinger that stops pretending its weapon is a fallback: Extra Attack at Wizard 6, Action Surge at character 8, then Divine Smite from character 10 turning 6th- to 9th-level Wizard slots into weapon burst. Pays for it with Spell Mastery, four Wizard levels of slot tier, and no shield while singing.

Menagerie.split: Wizard 17 (Conjuration) / Druid 2 (Circle of the Shepherd) / Cleric 1 (Tempest)
Menagerie.note: A summon chassis that cannot be knocked over — Focused Conjuration at Wizard 10 makes damage unable to break concentration on the set, the Wizard 6 off-list picks reach the druid pool, and Shepherd's Spirit Totems put a partner-facing aura under it. Cleric 1 supplies the heavy armour the school has none of.

Auspex.note: Portent dice spent through Lone Wolf's second reaction are guaranteed enemy-save failures or guaranteed misses, refunded on short rests from Wizard 6; the Knowledge domain adds double proficiency in Religion on an Intelligence body. No armour above medium and no at-will damage.

Lullaby.note: Hypnotic Gaze is charm-plus-incapacitate on one creature for no slot and no concentration, and in this list it strips the target's concentration too; Emboldening Bond puts a permanent d4 on both bodies' saves, which is what a d6 lockdown caster is short of. Split Enchantment doubles Hold Monster from character 11.

Pyroclast.note: The same school on a short-rest clock instead of a long-rest one: Consuming Fervor maximises a Fireball off a Channel Divinity charge that comes back twice a day, and Zeal's domain kit hands the robe heavy armour and martial weapons. Keeps Int/Wis saves by opening Wizard, so the save set is thinner than the Cleric-first evoker's.

Duskveil.note: The thinnest school bolted onto the strongest two-level opener available to it — Twilight Sanctuary is a no-action temp-HP tap on both bodies plus a charm and fright cleanse, on a short-rest charge, and Twilight 1 brings heavy armour, martial weapons and 90 m darkvision. The school itself contributes one attack-negation per rest and nothing that scales.

Charnel.note: The action-economy answer: Animate Dead++ removes the cap entirely, upcasts two more bodies per slot and extends Undead Thralls' HP and proficiency damage to every undead owned, none of it costing concentration. Grave 1 buys the save pair, a shield and a free bonus-action Spare the Dying for the run's actual failure mode.

Vantage.note: Scored as the generic Wizard list plus heavy armour and one mitigation reaction, because that is all the class file can confirm — the school's identity is a reaction AC and save spike that pairs with Lone Wolf's spare reaction, and War 1 adds the armour and a bonus-action attack the robe otherwise lacks.

Codex.note: Formulaic Attunement ignores resistance to the attuned damage type and adds damage on top, which is the rubric's named exemption from the Absolute Wrath cap and worth more here than its size suggests; the Spectral Mind is both a body and a remote casting position for a chassis with no third party member to stand in front of it.

Litany.note: The rescue ceiling of the class, and Disciple of Life from a single Cleric level boosts every one of its heals from any source. By character 11 it holds prevention (Erudite Remedy's chosen resistance, pre-appliable at 18 m), restoration (Lesser and Greater Restoration always prepared, Raise Dead as a ritual) and repeatable outward healing at once, with Spirit Guardians as real area denial under it.

Deathknell.note: The highest sustained single-target damage of the schools and the only one that converts Arcane Recovery charges into damage — Touch of Death is 5 plus twice Wizard level for two charges, roughly five times a long rest at Wizard 19, on top of Negative Energy Infusion and doubled necrotic cantrips. Inescapable Destruction strips necrotic resistance, which is what keeps a mono-type body off the Absolute Wrath cap.

Ordnance.note: Scored as the bare Wizard chassis plus a Cleric 1 armour grant, because that is the only part of this build that can be defended from source. The published identity is long-range ordnance, so the real profile is probably an AoE and single-target lift over this floor — but no number here is the subclass's.

Caprice.note: The 14228 list finally gives Wild Magic a control spine castable off sorcery points, and Bend Luck is a two-reaction, non-concentration swing on any roll in the fight — including the partner's saves. Emboldening Bond is the hedge: a permanent d4 on both bodies' saves is exactly what a chassis that triggers its own surges wants.

Aberrance.note: Psionic Sorcery casts Evard's, Hunger of Hadar and Dominate Person for sorcery points with no verbal or somatic components, turning the point pool into a second and cheaper casting clock; Psychic resistance plus advantage on Charm and Fright saves patches the two effects most likely to remove a body. Artificer 1 is the opener because it brings Int and Con saves, medium armour, shields and the Sleight of Hand the Araj gate is paid in.

Beatitude.note: The only Charisma caster that gets Cleric healing as Sorcerer spells, so Metamagic applies — Twinned Death Ward and Twinned Greater Restoration cover a two-body party outright, and Revivify plus Raise Dead answer the duo's worst failure mode. Paragon 1 upgrades Favored Soul's own medium armour to heavy and returns two feats.

Oriflamme.note: Mono because the level-20 capstone is the point: +4 to two stats, breaking the ceiling Lone Wolf and the ASI feat both stop at, and reachable only by pure Paragon 20. Banners count as attacks for Extra Attack, so post-5 you banner and swing; Legendary Banner at 17 hands the partner a free attack every turn for Charisma-modifier turns.

Emberwake.note: The debuff Paragon, mono for the same capstone reason. Searing Blade strips all resistances for three turns on a failed Con save — the rubric names it as one of the list's resistance strips — and Supernatural Dampening then blocks the target's healing and treats it as sunlit, which makes the partner's damage type stop mattering.

Adamance.note: The durability Paragon, mono for the level-20 capstone. Sheer Will's temp HP carries a flat damage reduction that lands after Lone Wolf's halving and is therefore worth double, Training From Hell adds non-magical physical resistance at 13, and Competitive Streak refunds Willpower Dice off the partner's natural 20s so the pool is fed by someone else's rolls.

Coronet.note: Mono for the capstone. Shifting Court swaps your position with the partner's off a Bonus Action once Actions Speak Louder is online, which is the direct answer to a duo's worst failure mode, and Fairy's Curse at 9 strips a crit target's Bonus Actions and Reactions and halves its movement — action-economy denial that costs no concentration and no slot.

Runeblade.note: The only genuinely single-stat body in the class and the only one that makes Charisma the attack stat — Scholar's Armament converts the main-hand weapon, and Spell Sword attacks count as cantrips that work with Extra Attack. Six Focuses by 17 is six damage types against Absolute Wrath's layered resistances; mono because the capstone is +4 Charisma above the ceiling on a chassis where Charisma is attack, damage and DC at once.

Stillwater.note: The pure-throughput pick, mono for the capstone. Falling Rain is a free-action melee attack riding every Willpower Die you already spend, so Lone Wolf's second Action doubles the Blade Skills and therefore doubles the free attacks; Beyond All Limits at 18 refills the pool every turn and Wisdom of Void turns one round a rest into guaranteed criticals.

Downpour.note: The same engine wired to a third Action instead of the capstone: Fighter 2 at characters 6–7 buys Action Surge and Second Wind, and every extra Action is another Blade Skill and therefore another free Falling Rain. Keeps Beyond All Limits at Paragon 18; loses the +4/+4 that only pure 20 reaches.

Tincture.note: The only subclass in the modlist that measurably pays down the 120-plus supply cost of long-resting: Restorative Reagents makes every elixir 2d6 outward temp HP and Lesser Restoration free, Chemical Mastery adds free Heal and Greater Restoration at 15. One Cleric level buys heavy armour and Disciple of Life, which boosts every heal the character casts from any source.

Carapace.note: The tankiest Artificer with a short-rest burst bolted on: Arcane Armor grants heavy armour at 3 and Extra Attack lands at 5, then Fighter 1–3 at characters 6–8 add Action Surge, a Fighting Style and superiority dice. Guardian's Thunder Gauntlets impose no-concentration disadvantage on anything that hits you while attacking someone else, and Perfected Armor yanks an attacker off the partner for a reaction Lone Wolf leaves spare.

Fusillade.note: Arcane Firearm is +1d8 on every spell from 5, the cannon is resummonable without a daily charge, and Fortified Position at 15 fields two of them at once; three Wizard levels on the same Intelligence stat add Sculpt Spells — which matters far more in a duo, where the partner is always inside your own Fireball — plus Arcane Recovery and a scroll library.

Gearheart.note: One stat drives attack, damage, spell DC, saves and Arcane Jolt uses; Extra Attack at 5 is at-will, the Steel Defender is a permanent third body that imposes disadvantage on attacks aimed at the partner, and Arcane Jolt is outward healing that rides the attack routine and costs no action. Fighter 1–3 at characters 6–8 add Action Surge and superiority dice on the same short-rest clock.

Cutpurse.note: Fast Hands plus Lone Wolf gives three Bonus Actions, and Fighter 5 supplies the Extra Attack the class never gets — four Action attacks, three off-hand strikes and Action Surge on top. It trades Thief's Reflexes (17), which the author himself warns breaks in inescapable combats and misbehaves with shared ally turns, for a level of the game the Rogue table does not otherwise reach. No area answer at all and nothing aimed at the partner.

Legerdemain.note: The only Rogue with a real control list, built out rather than left on the third-caster table: Wizard 5 pushes the pooled caster level to ten, so the Enchantment and Illusion picks are cast off 5th-level slots instead of 2nd. Magical Ambush at Rogue 9 gives every one of those spells Disadvantage on the target's saves while Hiding, and Cunning Action Hide makes that an at-will condition rather than a setup. Bladesong pays the AC and concentration bill a robe would not. Two casting-adjacent stats on one body is the cost, and there is nothing outward-facing.

Charlatan.note: The Charisma reading of the same subclass, and a different body rather than a different weapon: Dirty Tricks and Panache finally have a DC behind them, Hypnotic Stare is a permanent bonus-action minus one to a chosen enemy's saves that costs no resource and no concentration, and Gift of Will at Mesmerist 7 puts Charisma onto the partner's Wisdom saves. It gives up Reliable Talent's back half and almost all of the damage — this is a control body that happens to carry a rapier.

Bloodhound.note: The out-of-combat ceiling of the class, with the two things the Rogue skill rungs assume and the class cannot supply bolted on: Guidance at will and a permanent extra body from Wild Companion. Steady Eye, Reliable Talent and four Expertise picks put its Perception rolls in the twenties and clear Araj's pocket; Insightful Fighting is a repeatable no-ally Sneak Attack enabler and Eye for Weakness at 17 adds a flat 3d6 on top of it.

Stratagem.note: Master of Tactics turns Help into a Bonus Action, and with Lone Wolf's second Bonus Action this body can pick the other half of the party off the floor and still hand it Advantage in the same round, at will, forever. The Life dip supplies the healing the Rogue table has no version of — Disciple of Life on every Healing Word, Lesser Restoration, Guidance — and Soul of Deceit at 17 makes it immune to Charm. Its own damage is the price: no Extra Attack, ever, and it falls behind the act's par by Act III.

Gravewhisper.note: Whispers of the Dead grants proficiency in every skill of a chosen ability once per short rest, on demand, which is how one body covers whichever ability the act's gate turns out to sit behind. Wails from the Grave is the only Rogue answer to two targets at once and becomes full Sneak Attack on both at 17; the Echo is a second body that also eats a hit. Ghost Walk plus Uncanny Dodge plus Evasion is the deepest defensive stack on any Rogue here, and the Soul Trinket economy funds it from kills rather than from Listo's 120-supply long rests.

Outrider.note: Survivalist's free Expertise pair takes the body to six, and Ambush Master at 13 is +5 initiative plus a first-round mark that gives everyone Advantage on that target — a party-wide buff is worth double when the party is two. The Beast Master companion arrives with Companion's Bond already attached at Ranger 3, which is the cheapest permanent third body in the list, and Sudden Strike at 17 finally gives the chassis a second Sneak Attack per turn on a different target. Nothing here is aimed at the partner and nothing hits a crowd.

Mindblade.note: The most self-sufficient body in the batch — weapon, accuracy fix, mobility and invisibility all come out of one pool, so it needs no gear and no ally, and Homing Strikes only spends the die when the attack then hits. Fighter 3 buys the third Action and a short-rest manoeuvre pool the class has no version of. Rend Mind at 17 is the only hard Stun on any Rogue here. Thrown blades deal Psychic, which Absolute Wrath's layered resistances punish, so melee stays the main line.

Siphon.note: The counterspell-shaped Rogue. Arcane Strike is a Sneak Attack that always qualifies and lands as Force — the least-resisted type in the list — and Brilliant Edge at 13 adds Intelligence as Force to every weapon attack and makes that Force pierce Resistance. Auspicious Parry takes 1 damage instead of a hit, and Lone Wolf's second Reaction means you parry and still Uncanny Dodge. Bladesinging pays the Intelligence the kit already demands back as AC and Constitution saves. Its own fuel is the weak point: a pool of 1 + Int on a long rest, topped up only when enemies actually cast.

Lodestar.split: Paladin 17 (Oath of Devotion) / Bard 3 (College of Lore)
Lodestar.note: The plain, safe oath taken deep, with the class's one structural hole patched: Paladin scores a 1 on Skills in every act and Lore 3 buys four proficiencies and Expertise twice on a stat the oath already maxes. Aura of Devotion's charm immunity covers the partner at 9 m, Improved Divine Smite at 11 is the scaling rider that holds the damage rung, and Revivify plus Lay on Hands is the rescue floor. What it does not have is any area answer, any third attack source, or any reason to be preferred over the oaths that carry a second aura.

Greenmantle.split: Paladin 17 (Oath of the Ancients) / Sorcerer 3 (Draconic Bloodline)
Greenmantle.note: Aura of Warding at 7 is proportional resistance to spell damage covering both bodies at 9 m — this body's own mitigation layer and unconditional prevention aimed at the partner in one feature, against the damage type Listo's rebuilt casters lean on hardest. The Sorcerer three buys Font of Magic as a slot-to-point battery for smites and Twinned Spell, which in a two-person party makes every single-target buff a party buff. It is a defensive chassis: the damage is bare Extra Attack plus a smite, and the Skills column never moves off 1.

Enmity.note: Haste on the partner at Paladin 9 is the Actions ladder's top clause bought on a half-caster, and Twinned Spell turns it into Haste on both halves of the party for one sorcery point per slot level. Vow of Enmity is blanket Advantage on a short-rest charge, which is scale-invariant and worth more with Lone Wolf's doubled attack count than in a four-body party. The whole plan rides the one concentration slot, which is why it has no control of its own worth the name.

Reprisal.split: Paladin 12 (Oath of Vengeance) / Warlock 5 (The Fiend) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Reprisal.note: Oath of Vengeance run as a burst carry on a short-rest clock rather than as a support caster on a long-rest one. Two 3rd-level pact slots that come back on every short rest are smite fuel that a Paladin table cannot buy, Eldritch Smite is a repeatable burst channel rather than a slot spent, and Action Surge puts a third Action under Vow of Enmity's Advantage. It gives up Improved Divine Smite, Cleansing Touch and the whole 13-17 oath tier to get there.

Diadem.note: Champion Challenge is a no-concentration area taunt on a short-rest charge, which in a duo means pulling fire off the squishier half onto the body wearing heavy armour and holding the aura — and Spirit Guardians at oath level 9 makes standing in the middle of that crowd the damage plan as well. Peace's Emboldening Bond adds a second blanket save die on both bodies that stacks with the aura, and the domain brings Guidance the class otherwise lacks. Slow, static, and its Spirit Guardians is the pair's one concentration slot.

Nightsworn.split: Paladin 17 (Oathbreaker) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend, Pact of the Chain)
Nightsworn.note: Spiteful Suffering is a per-turn damage channel that also hands out Advantage on the target, stacked under Improved Unholy Smite and Aura of Hate; Animate Dead at oath level 9 plus Control Undead is real body count, and Pact of the Chain adds a familiar on top of it. Dreadful Aspect is area Frighten off a short-rest charge that spends no concentration. The cost is fixed and large: every smite is Necrotic and never Radiant, which is a straight downgrade against exactly the shadow-cursed and undead population it will spend Act II fighting.

Tyrant.note: The one oath whose capstone is worth twenty levels: Invincible Conqueror gives resistance to all damage, an extra attack and a 19-20 crit range for a minute, on the body already carrying heavy armour and the aura, and no three levels available elsewhere come close. Under it, Conquering Presence is area hard control on a short-rest charge that spends no concentration, Aura of Conquest taxes everything it lands on, and Guided Strike is +10 chosen after seeing the roll — a guarantee on the one attack that must land. Note the mod tags you as Oath of Vengeance for every oathbreaking trigger.

Bleakfire.split: Paladin 17 (Oath of the Bleak Walkers) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Bleakfire.note: Black Flames is a bonus-action burst channel on a short-rest charge that also Sickens the target's Constitution saves, and it upgrades to 2d10 plus 2d10 with a three-round bleed at oath level 15. The level 7 aura reduces the roll needed to crit for both bodies and stacks with the crit-range gear the list is full of. Expertise in Intimidation at level 1 clears Act I's Hag's Hair gate outright on a stat the oath already maxes — the only Skills rung anywhere in the paladin set. Death's Maw's flat proficiency-bonus reduction is real but flat, so it slides in a boss-weighted Act III.

Moonward.note: The most duo-tuned oath in the list, and the capstone is why it stays mono: Lunar Champion at 20 gives a third Reaction on top of Lone Wolf's second and hands both bodies a Charisma-modifier bonus to every saving throw stacked on the aura, plus temporary Freedom of Movement. Under it sit prevention in two forms at once — Aura of Moonlight's flat minus-Charisma on every hit either body takes, and Divine Guardian halving all damage on the partner for ten turns off a short-rest charge — with Full Moon as slot-free area Blind-and-Slow and Spirit Guardians at oath level 9. It is not a damage body and never becomes one.

Nightbloom.note: Oath of the Moon rebuilt around a short-rest clock rather than around a capstone. Twilight Sanctuary is a no-action aura that temp-HPs the partner every single round, and at Cleric 6 it comes back twice per short rest; Cleric 7 adds Death Ward, so this body carries prevention, restoration and a standing outward source at once. Paladin 13 still reaches the aura, Improved Divine Smite and Fount of Moonlight. It gives up Lunar Champion, Silvered Rebuke and four levels of slots, and it splits its casting across two stats.

Dawnwright.note: Scored as the bare paladin chassis plus a Light domain dip, because that is all that is verifiable — the oath has no published level-by-level feature list anywhere and Listo added the pack 'for testing'. The Light three at least makes the ranged-radiant pitch real without relying on the oath: Radiance of the Dawn is a repeatable area radiant burst on the short-rest Channel Divinity clock, Warding Flare imposes Disadvantage on an attack a few times a day, and Scorching Ray and Fireball come always prepared. Do not build a duo plan around the oath layer without confirming it in game.

Chronicler.note: The one chassis in the batch where staying is unambiguously right: Automatic Magical Secrets Extender turns the picks at 10, 14 and 18 into six spells drawn from every list the modlist installs, against a pool that reaches 415 by 18 — the largest single grant anywhere in Listo, and it is the last three levels that carry it. Under that, Lore's three bonus proficiencies on top of Bard's own three, Expertise four times, and Peerless Skill at 14 usable inside dialogue make this the body that clears the run's named gates. It has no armour worth the name and its own weapon damage is a rounding error.

Duskchant.note: College of Lore trades four levels of Magical Secrets for the two things a robe caster cannot buy: heavy armour and a partner-keeping engine. The Twilight domain hands a Charisma caster heavy armour and martial weapons at level one, and Twilight Sanctuary is a no-action aura that temp-HPs the other body every round — twice per short rest once the second Channel Divinity charge lands at Cleric 6. Peerless Skill and Expertise four times still arrive; the ninth-tier slots and the 18 Secrets do not.

Cadenza.note: Extra Attack at College level 6 with a Slashing Flourish rider, and Goon's interrupt versions of all three Flourishes convert both of Lone Wolf's Reactions into damage. Fighter 3 adds the third Action and a short-rest manoeuvre pool, and Master's Flourish at 14 rolls a d6 instead of spending Inspiration so the engine stops competing with the outward-facing use of the die. Medium armour and no shield is the whole defensive story, which is thin by Act III.

Ricochet.note: The thrown reading of College of Swords, and a genuinely different clock: Thrown Weapon Fighting is on the Swords style list thanks to UA Fighting Styles, the Slashing Flourish interrupt explicitly supports throwing, and Fast Hands on top of Lone Wolf's second Bonus Action means three thrown attacks a round outside the Action economy. Its damage has no rest clock at all, which is the top of Endurance by definition. It gives up Action Surge, the manoeuvre pool and any pretence of area control.

Bravura.split: Bard 17 (College of Valour) / Paladin 3 (Oath of Devotion)
Bravura.note: Valour is the cheapest way to make a Charisma caster durable — medium armour, shields and martial weapons at College level 3, with Combat Inspiration spending the die for AC on demand — and the Paladin three turns the full-caster slot table into smite fuel, so an 8th-level slot becomes burst weapon damage rather than a spell the pair has no concentration left for. Battle Magic at 14 hands a free weapon attack after every cast. No heavy armour and no aura: the Paladin levels arrive too late for either.

Pageant.note: Mantle of Majesty is a repeated Command that costs a bonus action and no concentration, which is the single-target control rung the College is actually good at, and Unbreakable Majesty at 14 is the best aggro-shed in the class in a run where losing one body ends the fight. The Peace dip supplies what Glamour never does for itself: medium armour and shields, Guidance, and Emboldening Bond's blanket save die on both bodies. Nothing in this College improves its own damage at all, and the 1s are real.

Honeyword.note: Two save-strippers that stack and neither of which costs concentration: Unsettling Words subtracts a rolled die from the target's next save and shows you the number before you commit the control spell, and Hypnotic Stare is a permanent bonus-action minus one on a chosen enemy for no resource at all. Unfailing Inspiration returns the die whenever the partner's roll fails, which in a duo — where the die always goes outward — is the most sustained Inspiration economy in the list. Towering Ego puts Charisma onto its own Wisdom saves. It has no armour and no damage.

Pirouette.note: A Dexterity martial with no weapon: Bardic Unarmed Attack is at-will and rides the Inspiration die to a d12 at 15, and Agile Strikes gives a free kick every time you inspire the partner, so Lone Wolf's two Bonus Actions become two free attacks a round. The College gets no Extra Attack at any level, which is its one structural hole, and Fighter 5 is the cheapest patch for it — plus Action Surge and a short-rest manoeuvre pool. It costs the 18 Magical Secrets and leaves the body in light armour.

Threnody.note: Sorrowful Fate converts any save the pair forces into a Charisma save, which is the stat most enemies are worst at, and Poetry in Misery refunds Inspiration on any natural 1 within 9 m — a Reaction-hungry College in a run where Lone Wolf grants a second Reaction, so Poetry in Misery and Tale of Hubris can both be live in the same round. The Sorcerer three adds Twinned Spell, which in a two-person party makes any single-target buff cover everyone, and Quickened for a third cast a turn. Nimbus of Pathos is a fight-ending button whose target drops to 0 HP when it ends, which in a duo is half the action economy.

Herald.note: Rallying Cry already makes Second Wind a short-rest outward heal for full Fighter level; Life 3 turns that into a real rescue block — Disciple of Life on every heal, Healing Word, Aid and Lesser Restoration — without touching the Inspiring Surge engine that hands the partner a reaction attack off Action Surge. Stops at 17 because Banneret's level-18 upgrade only adds a second ally a duo does not have.

Quarry.note: Volley at class 11 is the rubric's own Act II rung-5 AoE anchor — full weapon damage to every target, no save, no resource — and Lone Wolf's second Action fires it twice a round. By Act III the same button is only the act's ordinary at-will weapon AoE, which is the clearest single fall in this set; Colossus Slayer's flat +1d8 keeps single-target at par and no better.

Rime.note: Glaring Frost forces a Con save for Blind on every instance of Cold or Radiant damage, and the Paladin block at characters 4-6 is taken purely to supply that damage on demand — Divine Smite is Radiant, so every smite is a blind attempt, and the two half-caster tables stack to 5th-level slots. Snow Blindness then taxes every action a blinded enemy takes, and Snowborn Anthelion spreads the save to everything within 3 m.

Voltage.note: The armoured artillery build: Sculpt Spells means the partner is never inside the Fireball, Empowered Evocation from character 11 puts Intelligence on every evocation damage roll, and Cleric 1 fixes the AC the school never addresses. Zero rescue beyond a Cure Wounds off the shared slot pool.

Retort.note: Built around the one thing a Wizard can simply leave on the other player — the Transmuter's Stone granting Constitution save proficiency or a damage resistance, permanently and for no action — with Forge's long-rest blessing adding +1 AC or +1 weapon on top. Everything else in the school is a blue jay.

Malison.note: The only Wizard with at-will damage: four invocations by Wizard 10 on an Intelligence chassis, Eldritch Blast with Agonising Blast copied in as a Wizard spell, ritual completion paying temp HP equal to ritual level plus Wizard level, and flat immunity to the charm and fear line at Wizard 10. Cleric 1 supplies armour it has none of.

Wyrmline.note: An Amethyst ancestry puts Elemental Affinity's Charisma modifier on Force — every Magic Missile dart, and a damage type almost nothing in the list resists — while Paragon 1 returns two armour feats, heavy armour, shields and the Con/Cha save pair for a single caster level. Nothing aimed at the partner at all.

Squallborn.note: The classic stack, and the class file confirms it works here — Multiclass Preferred Casting Ability Fix keeps Charisma as the casting stat, so Tempest 1 buys heavy armour, martial weapons and Wrath of the Storm without splitting the primary. Heart of the Storm then bolts a free area rider onto every Lightning or Thunder cast, and Tempestuous Magic keeps the caster off the floor for a bonus action Lone Wolf has spare.

Nightfall.note: Hound of Ill Omen is the rung-4 shape on a short-rest clock — a summoned third body imposing disadvantage on one target's saves for no concentration, so it never competes with the partner's one spell. Strength of the Grave is a repeating refusal to go down, and Paragon 1 gives the d6 chassis heavy armour and a shield to refuse from behind.

Aetherblade.note: The same Charisma gish with real spellcasting instead of the capstone: Sorcerer 7 taken across characters 10–16 brings 4th-level slots, Twinned and Quickened, and Elemental Affinity adding Charisma to whichever Focus damage type the ancestry matches. It front-loads — pure Paragon 9 through Act I — and dilutes as the Sorcerer levels arrive.

Garrote.note: The alpha-strike stack: Listo's d10+Dex initiative, Gloom Stalker's +3 on top, Assassin's Alacrity handing back an Action and a Bonus Action at combat start, Dread Ambusher's extra first-round attack, and guaranteed crits on anything Surprised. It is the most front-loaded body in the batch and falls accordingly — against +170% boss HP the opener is a shrinking share of a long fight, and the chassis adds nothing once round one is over.

Flourish.note: Rakish Audacity means Sneak Attack lands without a flanking body, which is the exact hole a two-character party has, and Fancy Footwork means the walk in costs nothing. Swashbuckler has no subclass features at all from 13 to 20, so the last five levels go to Fighter for Extra Attack, Action Surge and Improved Critical rather than to a dead table. Dirty Tricks run off Charisma on a Dexterity body, so their DCs stay soft.

Aria.note: The only Bard College in the list that is a genuine blaster, paired with the one domain that maximises exactly the damage types it deals: Destructive Wrath is a Channel Divinity that maximises Lightning and Thunder, and at Cleric 6 that is two maximised bursts per short rest rather than one per long.
