Tempest also hands a Charisma caster heavy armour and martial weapons at level one. Electrifying Aria at College level 14 is a ten-turn persistent AoE that buffs the partner's crit rate while degrading enemy Constitution saves every turn, then converts into a mass Stun with Finale!. Everything it does is one of two damage types, which Absolute Wrath's layered resistances punish.

Bastion.note: A Divination Wizard normally spends its Portent dice from a robe. This one spends them from behind heavy armour and a shield: Paragon 1 is the only opener that hands a Wizard heavy armour, shields, martial weapons and two saves at once, and it returns two to three armour feats out of seven — which is what pays for Heavy Armour Master in Act I, where two feats is the whole budget. The school is unchanged; the body stops being the thing the encounter deletes first. It gives up the Knowledge domain's Expertise, so skills stay at the Wizard floor and there is no answer to a DC 25 in Act III.

Necromancy.note: The same undead engine, on a body that can also pass the checks. Rogue as the level-1 class — not as a dip — is the only way to buy four skills and Expertise ×2 for no feat, and Phantom's Whispers of the Dead grants proficiency in every skill of a chosen ability once per short rest, so the one body covers whichever ability the act's gate asks for. The cost is the armour: light only, no shield, and Grim Harvest is doing the work Cleric 1's heavy armour used to.

Interrogator.note: Order of Scribes is Formulaic Attunement and nothing else, and this body keeps the resistance-piercing while buying a named skill gate outright: Stern Gaze runs Intimidation off Wisdom, which is the only non-Charisma route to the Hag's Hair, and Vengeance's Monster Tactician grants Expertise in an Intelligence skill plus double Wisdom modifier on it. Inquisitor 1 also carries medium armour, shields, martial weapons and a two-charge short-rest Judgment. It trades heavy armour and a Charisma save for that.

Reliquary.note: A School of Death Wizard taken straight is the damage reading and has no defensive layer at all — the class file says so outright. This one buys the layer: Fighter 1 first for heavy armour, shields, Str and Con saves and Second Wind, Action Surge at character 2 for a third Action every short rest, and Battle Master's four superiority dice as a rest-cheap floor. Touch of Death and Negative Energy Infusion arrive three character levels later than they would without the dip, so Act I single-target is a rung thinner and the body is back-loaded.

Illusion.note: The thinnest school has one thing nobody used: it makes the enemy Surprised on demand. Assassinate turns any successful attack roll against a Surprised creature into a critical hit, and a spell attack roll is an attack roll — so Chromatic Orb, Scorching Ray and Disintegrate all crit out of Improved Minor Illusion and Greater Invisibility, on Listo's d10 initiative. Assassin's Alacrity refunds an Action and a Bonus Action at the start of every fight. It is front-loaded by construction and gives up Twilight Sanctuary's rescue entirely.

Tactician.note: Hierophant rescue with a skills answer bolted on. Erudite Remedy is a bonus action and Lone Wolf hands out two of those, so the healing stays and the other bonus action goes to Master of Tactics, which makes Help a bonus action — the partner comes off the floor without anyone spending an Action. Rogue as the level-1 class brings four skills, Expertise ×2 and Dex/Int saves for no feat. It gives up Disciple of Life's boost to every heal and Cleric 1's heavy armour.

Clockwork.note: An Enchantment Wizard holds the pair's one concentration slot on a body with no Constitution save and no bodies of its own. Artificer 1 is the only opener in the list that grants Intelligence and Constitution saves together — the exact pair a Hold Person chassis needs — and it comes with medium armour, shields and Sleight of Hand. Two infusions then do what no Cleric level can: Enhanced Arcane Focus is +1 to the spell save DC that Split Enchantment is doubling, and the Homunculus plus the Steel Defender are two permanent extra bodies. It gives up Emboldening Bond's d4 on both characters.

Grimoire.note: Hexcraft's invocations can be spent on at-will damage for the Wizard itself; this spends the same slot-economy school on the partner instead. Cutting Words and the school's reaction-fuelled slot recovery both want the Lone Wolf second reaction, Bardic Inspiration and Listo's Magical Inspiration let the partner spend a die on their own spell damage or healing, and Song of Rest is a resource in a run where a long rest costs 120 supplies. Lore is taken as the level-1 class, so it also brings six proficiencies, Expertise ×2 and Jack of All Trades for no feat.

Conjuration.note: Not the summon reading of the school but the one the Conjuration School Enhanced mod actually added: a bonus-action item conjurer that makes Alchemist's Fire, acid vials, grease bottles, caustic bulbs, healing potions and smokepowder bombs, scaling a die at levels 5, 10 and 15. Thief's Fast Hands on top of Lone Wolf's second bonus action is three conjure-and-throw bonus actions a round, which is a repeatable area engine and a persistent-surface control routine that spends no slot and no concentration — and thrown healing potions reach the partner. Everything it does is rest-free.

Duelist.note: Swashbuckler fixes the thing a Bladesinger in a duo actually lacks — a reason for Sneak Attack to apply. Rakish Audacity needs neither advantage nor a second melee body, which is the hole a two-person party is permanently in, and Rogue as the level-1 class also pays four proficiencies, Expertise ×2 and Dex/Int saves. Extra Attack arrives at character 9 rather than 6, so the body is back-loaded and Act I is a caster with a rapier.

Silvertongue.split: Wizard 17 (School of Bombardment) / Bard 3 (College of Eloquence)
Silvertongue.note: School of Bombardment can barely be defended from source, so the three off-levels go to what they can prove instead of to an armour grant: Eloquence's Silver Tongue means Persuasion and Deception cannot roll below 10, Expertise doubles them, and Jack of All Trades covers everything not picked — so one body clears the Act I Hag's Hair and the Act II pickpocket without a Charisma partner. Song of Rest carries the Endurance the Wizard table does not.

Evocation.note: Evocation with the Sorcerer's metamagic pointed at the partner rather than at a Channel Divinity clock. Twinned Spell in a two-person party covers everyone, so Twinned Haste out of the Wizard's own 3rd-level slots is the Act I rung-5 Actions clause bought with three levels, and Twinned Death Ward from character 10 is prevention on both bodies at once. Quickened converts an Action spell to a bonus action, which is the only reliable route to three casts a turn under Listo's bonus-action-spell rule. Font of Magic runs both directions off the Wizard's slot table, which is the fuel a Sorcerer 3 dip otherwise lacks. It gives up all armour except Draconic Resilience.

Greenward.note: The Wizard's real problem in a 120-supply run is that Arcane Recovery refreshes on a long rest and nothing else does — armoured artillery that runs dry. Land's Natural Recovery hands slots back on a short one. Druid 1 as the level-1 class also brings Int and Wis saves, medium armour and shields, Guidance at will, and Find Familiar always prepared from Wild Shape's companion clause, which is a permanent extra body for one level. Sculpt Spells still keeps the partner out of the Fireball.

Echoform.note: The Transmuter's Stone is the one thing this school can leave parked on the other player, and it stays parked. What Fighter 3 adds is that the body stops being the softer half of the pair while it does: Fighter 1 first for heavy armour, shields and Str/Con saves, Action Surge at character 2, and Manifest Echo as a second position the body can act from and swap to. The Echo is also the answer to Transmutation's real weakness — the school gives the caster nothing defensive of its own past level 6.

Deepwatch.note: The generic Wizard list with a Fiend pact bolted onto it, because Wizard slots only come back for 120 supplies. Warlock 2 buys short-rest slots, and at Warlock 3 they are 2nd level, spent three times a long-rest cycle. The Fiend adds temp HP on every kill and Pact of the Chain adds a permanent third body on the initiative order. Warlock 1 first also pays Wisdom and Charisma saves. There is no heavy armour on this body, and it keeps War Magic's reaction spike.

Sleuth.note: Abjuration spending its three multiclass levels on the coverage the Arcane Ward cannot buy: Rogue as the level-1 class is four proficiencies, Expertise ×2 and Dex/Int saves for no feat, and Inquisitive's Steady Eye is advantage on Perception and Investigation for the rest of the run — which is what the Act II hidden-content and Act III search gates actually ask for. Projected Ward still spends the Lone Wolf second reaction on keeping the partner up, and Improved Abjuration puts the pool on a short-rest clock. Spell Resistance arrives at character 17 rather than 14.

Ironsight.note: Inquisitive read as a weapon rather than as an out-of-combat ceiling: Insightful Fighting is a repeatable no-ally Sneak Attack enabler and Eye for Weakness adds a flat 3d6 on top of it, so the body wants Action Surge and a second attack far more than it wants Guidance. Fighter 1 first is heavy armour, shields, Str and Con saves and Second Wind; taking Rogue as the later class costs the level-1 Expertise pair and three proficiencies, which is what pays for it. Expertise returns at Rogue 6 and Reliable Talent at Rogue 11.

Cutlass.note: Swashbuckler has no subclass features from 13 to 20 — the class file is explicit — so the answer here is to stop at Rogue 11, where Reliable Talent and Cunning Strike are, and spend the nine levels the subclass cannot use on the half of the table Rogue never gets. Fighter 1 first buys heavy armour and Str/Con saves, Fighter 5 buys the Extra Attack that Sneak Attack has been waiting for, and Fighter 7's Brutish Durability is an unconditional d6 on every save with no resource behind it. Rakish Audacity still means no second melee body is required.

Sanctuary.note: A Phantom left alone has a Rescue column of straight zeroes, which in a duo means the other body has to carry every recovery in the run. Twilight is the fix and it costs three levels: Cleric 1 first is heavy armour from the domain, martial weapons, shields and Wis/Cha saves, and Cleric 2's Twilight Sanctuary is a no-action aura that temp-HPs the partner every round and clears Charm and Fright, on a Channel Divinity that returns on a short rest. Whispers of the Dead still covers whichever ability the act's gate asks for. What it loses is the Rogue level-1 skill package, so the proficiency count is thin and the coverage is all on-demand.

Steelmind.note: Arcane Trickster read as the Intelligence half-caster it nearly is, rather than as a controller: Artificer 1 as the level-1 class is the only opener granting Intelligence and Constitution saves together, plus medium armour, shields and Sleight of Hand, and it uses the same casting stat the subclass already needs. Two infusion slots then buy Enhanced Arcane Focus for the spell DC, Enhanced Defense for the AC, and a Homunculus — which with the Steel Defender and the permanent invisible Mage Hand puts three extra bodies on the field for a Rogue. The control ceiling drops in exchange.

Adjudicator.note: Half of Mastermind is written in Wisdom — Insightful Manipulator's save penalty, Unerring Eye's uses, Soul of Deceit's bonus to Deception — and a Dexterity Rogue with a Life-domain dip has none of it. Inquisitor 1 as the level-1 class puts Wisdom on the sheet and pays for it: martial weapons, medium armour, shields, Wis and Str saves, a two-charge short-rest Judgment, and Righteous Vigilance stacking Wisdom onto initiative. Stern Gaze runs Intimidation off Wisdom for the Hag's Hair, and Vengeance's Monster Tactician is Expertise in an Intelligence skill with double Wisdom modifier on it — but on a Dexterity Rogue with neither Intelligence nor Wisdom on the sheet, that doubled modifier has almost nothing to double. It gives up Cleric outward healing entirely and has almost no Rescue.

Chorus.note: A Fiend Warlock taken straight is a burst engine that reads 1 on skills, which in a two-person run means the partner has to be the entire face and the entire toolbox. Bard as the level-1 class is the same Charisma the Warlock already needs — no second stat, no MAD — and it returns Dex and Cha saves, three proficiencies, Lore's three more, Expertise ×2, Jack of All Trades over everything else, Song of Rest and Bardic Inspiration the partner can spend on their own spell damage under Listo's Magical Inspiration. Dark One's Blessing and the expanded fire list survive; the Zeal domain's maximised Fireball and its heavy armour do not.

Oathbound.split: Warlock 14 (The Great Old One) / Paladin 6 (Oath of the Ancients)
Oathbound.note: A Great Old One control specialist on its own sits at 1 on Durability and 0 on Rescue, which is a body the enemy AI will pick first and the partner cannot pick back up. Six Paladin levels taken first invert exactly that: heavy armour and Wis/Cha saves at level 1, Divine Smite converting short-rest pact slots into burst, Extra Attack and Revivify at 5, and Aura of Protection at 6 — the Charisma modifier added to every saving throw both bodies make, at Listo's 9m radius. Mortal Reminder still fires off crits, and there are more of them now. The cost is Mystic Arcanum 8th and 9th and the Entropic Ward line arriving late.

Fontspark.note: Three Sorcerer levels on the Warlock's own Charisma, spent entirely on the partner: in a two-person party Twinned Spell covers the entire party — Twinned Death Ward from character 10 is prevention on both bodies at once, Twinned Greater Invisibility is both bodies untargetable, and Quickened is the only reliable route to a third cast in a turn under Listo's bonus-action-spell rule. Font of Magic converts short-rest pact slots into sorcery points and back, which is the fuel a three-level Sorcerer otherwise does not have. Fey Presence is still slot-free area control. The armour goes: Draconic Resilience and light armour is all of it.

Chorus of Fangs.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Beast) / Bard 3 (College of Lore)
Chorus of Fangs.note: The outward reading of the Beast. Call the Hunt at Barbarian 14 hands the partner +1d6 once per turn for the whole Rage, and Bard 1–3 taken at characters 6–8 buys Expertise ×2, Jack of All Trades, Song of Rest and six proficiencies at no feat cost — the first Barbarian in the file with a skills answer. It gives up Action Surge and the ninth swing that comes with it. Nothing on the Bard list survives entering a Rage, so those levels are a skills-and-Inspiration purchase, never a casting one.

Longstride.note: Rogue at level 1 is the only route to Expertise on a Barbarian — taken as a later multiclass it grants light armour and one skill and nothing else. The price is the Str+Con save pair, and Lone Wolf's two picks restore Constitution. Thief's second bonus action is what Mighty Impel and Boot of the Giants have always wanted, since Rage already claims one of the two. Extra Attack slips to character 8 and Demiurgic Colossus to 17; Unarmoured Defence still works, because it is a feature rather than a proficiency.

Bondwarden.note: Two pair-scope blanket boosters on one body: Peace's Emboldening Bond and Wild Magic's Goon-fixed Magic Awareness, which hands the proficiency bonus to both bodies' saves against spells. Bolstering Magic gives the partner a free slot or a d3 every rest cycle on top. Emboldening Bond is bonded out of combat for ten minutes and survives entering a Rage; every other Cleric spell on the sheet does not, which is why the dip is one level and not three. Gives up Primal Champion, Action Surge and the Str+Con pair.

Ghostfeint.split: Rogue 3 (Assassin) / Barbarian 17 (Path of the Ancestral Guardian)
Ghostfeint.note: Feral Instinct's +3 initiative and cannot-be-Surprised is exactly the platform Assassin wants, and Rogue at level 1 is the only way a Barbarian ever buys Expertise ×2 and four proficiencies. Ancestral Protectors still arrives at character 6 — a no-concentration mark that gives the struck creature Disadvantage on everything not aimed here and halves what it does land — and Spirit Shield at 9. What is gone is Paragon's armour package, the Willpower Dice and the Str+Con pair; the Act I burst also fades once round one stops deciding fights.

Grave Herald.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Revenant) / Bard 3 (College of Valour)
Grave Herald.note: A Revenant cannot be healed by any means, so every point of the partner's Rescue budget aimed at it is wasted — the honest answer is to spend the last three levels handing value outward instead of buying more armour. Bardic Inspiration, Song of Rest and Expertise ×2 land at characters 6–8; Ghost Armor already supplies the heavy armour proficiency at Barbarian 3, so nothing is lost by not opening Fighter. Haunt mirrors every point taken onto a Frightened target from character 6. Gives up Battle Master's dice.

Bonded Bulwark.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Juggernaut) / Monk 3 (Way of the Friar)
Bonded Bulwark.note: Friar's bond puts +1d4 on every saving throw both bodies make and streams temp HP to the partner each turn on a ki clock, sitting on top of Resolute Stance's at-will Disadvantage on every attack aimed here and Hurricane Strike's free reaction attack for the partner. Monk 1–3 at characters 6–8 costs no feat; what it costs is Action Surge and Battle Master's dice, so the damage sits a rung under what a Fighter dip would have bought and the skills stay at zero — this body asks its partner to carry every proficiency.

Endless Null.note: No dip at all, and the argument is mechanical rather than aesthetic. Magic Syphoning refreshes only when you spend a bonus action to enter a Rage, and the level-20 capstone returns a Rage charge every turn — so a once-per-Rage counterspell becomes a once-per-turn one. Primal Champion's +4 Constitution to a cap of 24 raises the Syphoning check and Herald of Ginnungagap's DC off the same stat, and Spell Eater turns every successful spell save into 2d6. The cost is Fighter 1's heavy armour and Action Surge, and a skills column that stays empty.

Ironbriar.note: Battlerager Armor already locks the body into medium metal armour, so Unarmoured Defence was never the loss it looks like — and Forge's Blessing of the Forge puts +1 AC on that armour after every long rest, with Wis+Cha saves and Sleight of Hand thrown in for the one level. A Thief dip to free the spike attack would be redundant: Lone Wolf already grants two bonus actions, which is enough for Rage and the spike in the same turn. The 1d4 spike and Spiked Retribution's flat 3 are what decay after Act I.

Sirocco.split: Rogue 3 (Swashbuckler) / Barbarian 17 (Path of the Storm Herald)
Sirocco.note: Storm Herald's Desert aura rather than its Tundra one. The aura is re-triggerable as a bonus action every turn and costs no rest resource, which makes it the only repeatable AoE source anywhere in the Barbarian file — but it is a flat 2/3/4/5 and therefore the clearest case in this set of a rung lost to +126% enemy HP. Rogue at level 1 buys Expertise ×2 and four proficiencies, and Shielding Storm still hands the partner fire resistance at Barbarian 10. Gives up the temp-HP stream that makes Tundra an outward aura.

Bannerbeast.note: Wolf Heart hands the partner Advantage on attacks against anything near you, and Bear Attunement at 14 is a genuine taunt — the two Wildheart choices that face the pair rather than the Barbarian's own Rage-gated capstone. Lionheart's Banner suite stacks a second outward layer on top, with a Fighting Style and two short-rest Willpower Dice. Taken after Barbarian 1 the Paragon levels bring no heavy armour and no saves, which costs nothing: a raging Barbarian cannot wear heavy armour anyway. The price is Primal Champion and unlimited Rage.

Stormpick.split: Rogue 3 (Thief) / Barbarian 17 (Path of the Lightning Vessel)
Stormpick.note: Lightning Reflexes at Barbarian 10 adds the full Constitution modifier to every Dexterity check, and Constitution is already this subclass's primary — put Rogue Expertise on Sleight of Hand on top and one body clears Araj's potion in Act II and the Circus music box in Act III, the two gates that are paid in Sleight of Hand and nothing else. Thief's second bonus action is the file's own named fix for three Galvanic Heart powers competing for one. Gives up Battle Master's dice and the Str+Con save pair.

Warchant.note: Frenzied Strike plus Lone Wolf's two bonus actions is already two extra swings a round and Retaliation adds two reaction attacks at 14, so the last three levels do not need to buy more damage. Swords brings medium armour, a Fighting Style and Blade Flourishes; Bard 3 brings Expertise ×2, Jack of All Trades and Song of Rest. Barbarian stays the level-1 class rather than opening on Fighter, so Str+Con and the d12 survive — and unlike a bare rager, this body can pass a check.

Godsworn Vigil.split: Barbarian 17 (Path of the Zealot) / Paladin 3 (Oath of the Ancients)
Godsworn Vigil.note: The insurance reading rather than the damage one. Warrior of the Gods lets the partner stand this body back up without spending a Revivify scroll, Rage Beyond Death at 14 makes it unkillable inside a Rage, and Fanatical Focus rerolls a failed save every Rage rather than every rest. Paladin 3 adds Lay on Hands aimed outward, Divine Sense and a Channel Oath on a short-rest clock. Divine Fury already supplies the per-hit rider, so the split costs Battle Master's dice and buys the pair's floor instead.

Auric Vigil.note: War is the only domain with a true Extra Attack, so a Fighter block spent on swing count would only be buying what the domain already gives. Six Paladin levels taken at characters 2–7 buy Aura of Protection instead — the Charisma modifier on every saving throw both bodies make — plus Extra Attack at character 6, Lay on Hands aimed outward and Divine Smite riding the War Priest bonus strike. The cost is the domain capstone, Cleric 15–17's prepared count, and a second stat that has to be raised.

Quietus.note: Peace's list has no area control whatsoever, and a Fighter 2 dip would do nothing about it. Three Wizard levels at characters 6–8 open scroll scribing and with it Grease and Web — Grease costs no concentration, which matters because the pair holds exactly two slots and Emboldening Bond wants neither. The bond still runs permanently on two bodies and Protective Bond still moves a killing hit onto the durable half. Gives up Action Surge and Cleric 18's third Channel Divinity charge, and the weapon column stays empty.

Anvilcant.note: Forge is the one domain that hands out Sleight of Hand at level 1, which is the proficiency both mid-run gates are paid in, and nobody spent it. Lore's three extra picks with Expertise ×2 and Jack of All Trades on top — Guidance is already on the Cleric list — makes this the pair's whole utility budget in one body, with Religion Expertise pointed at the Mirror's DC 25. Bard at characters 6–8 keeps Hag's Hair in reach. Soul of the Forge's +1 AC still lands at Cleric 6 and Saint of Forge and Fire at 17; the cost is Fighter's Action Surge and Cleric 18.

Errant Sign.note: Eldritch is the one domain granting no heavy armour and no martial weapons, so opening Cleric buys only the Wis+Cha save pair — trade it for Rogue 1's four proficiencies, Expertise ×2 and Dex+Int saves, and let Lone Wolf's picks restore Wisdom and Constitution. Nothing that makes the domain work is lost: Eldritch Contagion, Prophecy of Doom and Unpredictable Inspiration's re-selectable free cantrip and free skill all come through the multiclass node. Gives up Action Surge and the level-18 Channel Divinity charge.

Pyreheart.note: The caster reading of Hazoret. Consuming Fervor maximises Fire or Thunder twice per short rest from Cleric 6, the domain list already carries Fireball, Flame Strike and Destructive Wave, and three Sorcerer levels add Quickened and Heightened on top. Haste is a domain spell, so Twinned puts the extra Action on the partner and keeps one for itself. There is no weapon routine underneath any of it — no Extra Attack, no Battle Master dice — and Sorcerer 3 gives the tools without the fuel at three sorcery points.

Umbral Watch.split: Cleric 17 (Twilight) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One · Pact of the Chain)
Umbral Watch.note: The darkness body the Twilight domain was built for. Eyes of Night gives 90 m darkvision and the sanctuary makes you immune to overlapping magical darkness inside it, so Devil's Sight plus Darkness means the pair fights inside a sphere every enemy has to shoot into blind. Twilight Sanctuary still taps temp HP into both bodies each round off a short-rest charge and ends one charm or fright a turn; Pact of the Chain adds a third body on the initiative order. Gives up Fighter 5's Extra Attack and every swing that would have come with it.

Sparkstep.note: The Infiltrator model instead of the Guardian. Lightning Launcher counts as a ranged weapon, so Sneak Attack rides it, and Perfected Armor at Artificer 9 makes everything it hits glimmer — Disadvantage on that creature's attack rolls and +1d6 on yours, rising to advantage against it at 15. Thief's second bonus action stacks on Lone Wolf's. Arcane Armor still supplies heavy armour, but a launcher needs empty hands so there is no shield, and Battle Master's dice and Action Surge are both gone.

Emplacement.note: Pure twenty, with no three-level Wizard dip. Fortified Position at 15 fields two cannons on one action, level 18 brings six infusion slots and twelve known so the Homunculus rides alongside them, and Soul of Artifice at 20 adds +1 to every save and a reaction that refuses the drop to 0. That is a four-body party out of one character. The trade is the wider Wizard list and Evocation's sculpting — and the cannon's flat statline is the file's own worked example of a feature that stops mattering, which is why the damage columns sit where they do.

Wardsmith.note: Twilight Sanctuary is a per-round temp-HP tap on both bodies off a Channel Divinity charge a short rest refunds, and it ends one charm or fright per turn — the two losses a two-person party cannot absorb. Its size is 1d6 + Cleric level, so a three-level dip buys the clock rather than the number, which is the right purchase here. The domain also carries the heavy armour and martial weapons Artificer never gets. Arcane Jolt's outward 4d6 and the Steel Defender's Deflect Attack are untouched; the cost is Action Surge, Battle Master's dice and Magic Item Savant's second +1.

Alchemist.note: The Artificer multiclass node keeps Sleight of Hand, medium armour, shields and firearms and drops only the saves and the two skill picks — so opening Rogue costs almost nothing and buys four proficiencies, Expertise ×2 and Dex+Int saves, with Lone Wolf's picks restoring Wisdom and Constitution. Sleight of Hand ends up doubled at Artificer 6 and Guidance is already on the list, which is what four identically-scored Artificers were all missing. The elixir and supply economy is unchanged; what is gone is Life's Disciple of Life on every heal.

Totemsong.split: Druid 17 (Circle of the Shepherd) / Bard 3 (College of Lore)
Totemsong.note: Druids in this roster read 1.0 on skills; this one spends its three off-levels on Bard rather than on a Cleric domain: Expertise ×2, Jack of All Trades over everything it did not pick, three Lore proficiencies and Song of Rest, on a body that had Guidance nowhere and now has a College. The summon engine is native to the circle and survives untouched; what is given up is Disciple of Life on every heal, so the Flumph and Bear totems have to carry the outward healing alone.

Twinwrath.note: A Tempest dip would maximise this body's own damage. Storm Sorcery takes Metamagic instead and spends its turns on the other character: Twinned Haste covers a two-person party entirely for one point per slot level, Twinned Death Ward is prevention on both halves at once, and Font of Magic turns Druid slots into points and back. Wrath's own aspect damage stays, minus Destructive Wrath, and the body loses heavy armour and a full rung of Endurance to pay for it.

Dreamsworn.note: The one route in the list that lets a Wisdom body clear the Charisma gates. Stern Gaze runs Intimidation off Wisdom, which is the only non-Charisma answer to Hag's Hair DC 20, and Vengeance's Monster Tactician grants Expertise in an Intelligence skill plus double Wisdom modifier on it. Righteous Vigilance stacks Wisdom onto initiative on top of Dexterity. The cost is a Cleric dip's outward healing and any pretence of a damage line.

Stormlore.note: Same class, different domain, and the domain is the whole argument. Knowledge's Blessings of Knowledge is two Intelligence proficiencies with Expertise in both, and the Cleric brings Guidance at will, which no Druid outside the Stars has. Storm Shift still carries 54 temporary hit points at Druid 18 and the level 10 immunity-to-resistance clause is untouched; what goes is Destructive Wrath, so the lightning stops being maximised and the AoE drops a rung.

Frostfriar.split: Druid 17 (Circle of Winter) / Monk 3 (Way of the Friar)
Frostfriar.note: A Cold controller built as the pair's floor rather than as a damage line: Way of the Friar bonds the two bodies, temp-HPs both every turn at no action cost, gives both +1d4 on every saving throw, and hands over a free teleport to the partner. Winter Spirit stacks 85 temporary hit points on top of that and the level 10 prone-on-failed-Cold-save clause keeps the area control. Nothing here raises the damage line at all.

Wildsmite.split: Druid 17 (Circle of the Moon) / Paladin 3 (Oath of Vengeance)
Wildsmite.note: Circle of the Moon read as a melee body rather than as a caster keeping a beast form for a spare health bar: the Wild Shape Overhaul keeps multiclass features working inside the form, so Divine Smite fires off Druid slots on every beast attack, Wild Strike supplies the second attack, and Vow of Enmity buys advantage on a short-rest charge. Charisma is left at 10 because none of that needs a DC. The spell list is the price — you cannot cast while you are the bear.

Sporeward.split: Druid 18 (Circle of the Spores) / Cleric 2 (Twilight Domain)
Sporeward.note: Twilight rather than a manoeuvre pool: the domain grants heavy armour and martial weapons to a class that normally has neither, and Twilight Sanctuary is a no-action aura that temp-HPs the other character every single round off a short-rest Channel Divinity. That makes the melee Druid the pair's floor rather than just a harder hitter. Symbiotic Entity's 68 temporary hit points stack under the plate. The Extra Attack from 4018 and Spreading Spores are untouched; what goes is the manoeuvre pool and the Action Surge.

Emberchain.split: Druid 17 (Circle of Wildfire) / Warlock 3 (Pact of the Chain)
Emberchain.note: Wildfire without the healing. This body drops the healing entirely and stacks bodies instead: the Wildfire Spirit, a Pact of the Chain imp, Wild Companion's familiar and a Conjure Animals set that costs no concentration and lasts until long rest. Four independent actors on the initiative order is the largest count a Druid can field, and the spirit doubles as a second point of origin for every AoE. Charisma stays dumped, so the invocations are Armour of Shadows, Fiendish Vigour and Devil's Sight rather than Agonizing Blast.

Moonthief.note: A Circle of the Moon body whose control comes from the Rogue side rather than from a short-rest dice pool. Five levels of Rogue buy something the roster does not have anywhere else on a Druid: Cunning Strike, a Prone or Poison or Disarm rider that lands every turn, costs no action and spends no concentration — the rubric's own rung-4 clause for single-target control. Sneak Attack scales with dice rather than sitting flat, Swashbuckler removes the advantage requirement a duo cannot reliably meet, and the Wild Shape Overhaul keeps all of it working inside the beast form. The cost is two Druid levels and the level 14 circle tier.

Tidesong.split: Druid 17 (Circle of the Sea) / Bard 3 (College of Swords)
Tidesong.note: Wrath of the Sea already spends the bonus action every turn for Wisdom-scaled damage and a push, so the dip has nothing to add there. Swords adds a Fighting Style, scimitar proficiency and Blade Flourishes to make the weapon half real, and — the actual reason — Expertise ×2 and Jack of All Trades on a body that otherwise reads 1.0 on skills like every other Druid in the roster. Tempest's maximised thunder goes, and with it a rung of outward healing.

Landsong.split: Druid 17 (Circle of the Land) / Bard 3 (College of Lore)
Landsong.note: The bare Druid chassis, opened in class rather than through Fighter for heavy armour and Action Surge. Natural Recovery stays as the only in-day slot refund the class has, and the three spare levels go to Song of Rest and Expertise ×2 — the two things that raise the axes Lone Wolf makes worst. Endurance becomes the best row on the sheet. The price is heavy armour, the third Action, and two save proficiencies that swap from Strength and Constitution to Intelligence and Wisdom.

Starflare.split: Druid 18 (Circle of the Stars) / Cleric 2 (Light Domain)
Starflare.note: Circle of the Stars read as a radiant damage platform rather than as a support engine: Radiance of the Dawn is a repeatable area burst on the short-rest Channel Divinity clock that does not hit allies, Starry Form Archer fires a Wisdom-scaled radiant arrow off the bonus action every turn, and Star Maps hand over free Guiding Bolts. Warding Flare covers the reaction. Cosmic Omens stay on their short rest, but the outward healing collapses without Disciple of Life.

Loreshot.note: The Arcane Shot engine does not need a third body — it is already repeatable no-concentration control on a short-rest clock — so the three levels go to Lore rather than to a Beast Master companion: Expertise ×2, three bonus proficiencies, Jack of All Trades, Song of Rest, and Cutting Words to spend Lone Wolf's second reaction on. A Fighter also gets the Hag's Hair check at Intimidation DC 15 with advantage rather than DC 20, which Expertise turns into a formality. What goes is the companion, and with it a rung of action economy.

Portentblade.note: A mono Eldritch Knight scores a flat zero on Rescue for twenty levels — nothing it does ever touches the other character. Three Wizard levels on the stat this body already runs fix that with Portent: two dice rolled at dawn that replace any roll, so the partner's failed Wisdom save simply does not happen, or the boss's does. Arcane Recovery adds a short-rest slot refund and scroll transcription turns Listo's drops into a permanent library on an Intelligence body. The fourth attack at Fighter 20 is the price.

Giantwrath.split: Fighter 17 (Rune Knight) / Barbarian 3 (Path of the Berserker)
Giantwrath.note: A Rune Knight read as pure floor rather than as a skills platform: Rage stacks proportional resistance to all three physical types under heavy armour, Heavy Armour Master and Hill Rune, and Danger Sense joins Frost Rune to cover Dexterity and Constitution saves between them. Rage costs nothing here because a Rune Knight casts nothing. The trade is stark and deliberate — not one of the three off-levels was spent on a proficiency, and the out-of-combat column reads empty.

Mindpiercer.note: A Psi Warrior read as a controller rather than as a protector: the twelve psionic dice are a Prone-and-push routine that fires off every Psionic Strike, costs no concentration and never competes with the partner's one spell slot — and Hypnotic Stare bolts a permanent bonus-action penalty to one enemy's saving throws underneath it for no resource at all. Protective Field still exists, but the reaction is now being spent on the enemy rather than on the partner.

Bannerhold.note: A Cavalier protector that points its support outward in an unusual currency: Order's Voice of Authority means every buff or heal cast on the other character hands them an immediate weapon attack, so a Bless or a Cure Wounds is not a lost turn but a shared one. Unwavering Mark supplies a bonus-action attack of the body's own and Order's Demand adds a short-rest area effect. Order carries no healing aura, so the outward healing is bare long-rest slots — which is fine, because casting them is now the point.

Friarblade.split: Fighter 17 (Battle Master) / Monk 3 (Way of the Friar)
Friarblade.note: This body leaves the mono Battle Master's zero on skills unfixed and buys the pair's floor instead: the Friar bond temp-HPs both characters every turn at no action cost, gives both +1d4 on every saving throw, grants shield proficiency and a free teleport to the partner. Under heavy armour with Heavy Armour Master that is a body that is very hard to remove and keeps the other one standing, and the manoeuvre pool still runs the short-rest control. It carries no proficiencies at all, so the partner has to.

Blackfont.split: Paladin 17 (Oath of the Bleak Walkers) / Sorcerer 3 (Draconic Bloodline)
Blackfont.note: Three Sorcerer levels sit on the Paladin's existing Charisma and turn the body outward rather than inward: Twinned Death Ward and Twinned Greater Restoration cover a two-person party completely for one point per slot level — the rubric says outright that a Sorcerer 3 dip buys a Rescue rung that costs other chassis six levels — and Font of Magic converts spare slots into points and back into smite fuel. Quickened Spell is the only reliable route to three casts in a turn. The price is paid on the martial side: no Action Surge, no manoeuvre dice, and Endurance drops with them.

Moonsong.split: Paladin 17 (Oath of the Moon) / Bard 3 (College of Lore)
Moonsong.note: Taken mono for Lunar Champion, this oath reads 1 on skills for twenty levels. Three levels of Lore are fully Charisma-SAD on a paladin, so nothing is diluted: Expertise ×2, three bonus proficiencies, Jack of All Trades over everything else, Song of Rest, and Cutting Words for Lone Wolf's second reaction. Aura of Moonlight, Divine Guardian and Full Moon are all in place by Paladin 7 and none of them needs level 20. What is surrendered is precisely the capstone — the third Reaction and the party-wide Charisma bonus to every saving throw.

Silvercrit.note: The oath rebuilt around the swing rather than around a short-rest sustain clock. Action Surge is a third Action on a body that already has two, Improved Critical's 19–20 doubles Divine Smite dice and Fount of Moonlight's +2d6 radiant on every melee attack, and Remarkable Athlete's +3 initiative gets the burst in first. The oath's defensive half is untouched below Paladin 7 — Aura of Moonlight and Divine Guardian are still there — but without a Twilight dip there is no every-round temp HP, and the sustain sits a rung lower for it.

Ironchoir.note: Invincible Conqueror is the best capstone in the class, and this body sells it for Voice of Authority, which turns every levelled spell cast on the other character into an immediate free weapon attack for them — Bless, Aid, Shield of Faith and Heroism all become half of a shared turn rather than a lost one, and none of them needs a save DC the Wisdom stat cannot supply. Spiritual Weapon adds a bonus-action attack, Order's Demand a short-rest area effect. The frighten engine and Aura of Conquest are unchanged; the resistance-to-all-damage minute is not.

Wyrmwarden.note: A Draconic Bloodline taken straight is a pure damage specialist that scores a flat zero on Rescue in all three acts — nothing it does ever reaches the other character. Twilight fixes both of that bloodline's structural problems at once: the domain hands a d6 no-armour class heavy armour and martial weapons, and Twilight Sanctuary is a no-action aura that temp-HPs the partner every single round off a short-rest Channel Divinity, which is the rubric's own named Act I rung-4 rescue. Elemental Affinity still puts Charisma on every Force dart. Two levels of Sorcerer and Draconic Presence at 18 are the bill.

Dawnblind.note: Snowlight needs a Cold or Radiant source or it does nothing, and buying that source in Paladin smites would run it off Charisma — a stat the conclave never otherwise uses. Light buys it off Wisdom, the Ranger's own casting stat, so one DC serves both halves. Radiance of the Dawn is a short-rest area radiant burst that spares allies, which means every creature it touches rolls Glaring Frost's Constitution save or is Blinded, and Snowborn Anthelion at 15 spreads that save three metres from each of them. Snow Blindness then charges radiant damage on every action a blinded enemy takes. Blinding a room repeatedly on a short-rest clock is what this body does; the single-target smite damage is what it gives up to do it.

Polymath.note: Paragon's last three levels can go to the capstone and read 1 on the axis the model weights 2.5. This body spends them on College of Lore instead, taken at characters 6-8 so Expertise x2, Jack of All Trades, Lore's three bonus proficiencies and Song of Rest are all live for the Hag's Hair. It keeps Sheer Will's flat reduction and Training From Hell, and gives up Paragon 18's Beyond All Limits, the three-attack window and +4/+4 — so single-target sits a rung lower for a skills axis that moves three.

Vesper.note: Spellblade's off-levels can go on Sorcerer slots; these three buy a floor instead. Cleric 1-3 at characters 6-8 lands Twilight Sanctuary while Act I is still being fought, which is the one rung-4 rescue a Charisma martial can reach without becoming a caster, and the domain's heavy armour duplicates what Paragon 1 already gave so nothing is wasted on it. Spellblade stays whole through 17 — six Focuses, Magic Resistance at 9, Will Over Weave at 13 — so the trade is Sorcerer's 4th-tier slots and Twinned for a partner-keeping aura and a spell-save booster.

Bower.note: Paragon 20 ends in a capstone that raises its own two stats; this body spends those last three levels raising both bodies instead. Peace 1 at character 6 is Emboldening Bond, a permanent d4 on every attack, check and save the pair makes, and Balm of Peace puts outward healing on the short-rest clock the run actually runs on. Shifting Court still pulls the partner out of a pack on a bonus action, so the pair's floor is the whole point and the ceiling is the partner's problem. It gives up +4/+4 and the Butterfly Tempest finisher.

Almsgate.split: Paragon 17 (Sword Saint) / Monk 3 (Way of the Friar)
Almsgate.note: Falling Rain wired to the pair rather than to a third Action. Friar 3 at characters 6-8 costs the same three levels Fighter 2 nearly did and returns Friar's Bond — per-turn temp HP on both bodies and a +1d4 on every attack roll and saving throw either of them makes — plus a bonus-action teleport to the partner's side, which a heavy-armour body otherwise has no way to buy. Falling Rain still rides every Willpower Die, so the engine is intact; what is lost is Action Surge, Second Wind and the whole of Paragon 18-20.

Cinderquill.note: The one Paragon corner that has to be paid for at character level 1: Rogue first, because four proficiencies and Expertise x2 exist nowhere else, and a Paragon otherwise reads 1 out of combat for twenty levels. The bill is heavy armour and the Con/Cha save pair — this body is medium armour and shields for the whole run, and takes Dex/Int from Rogue with Lone Wolf covering Wis and Con. In exchange Searing Blade's resistance strip rides a Sneak Attack floor and a second bonus action, and Vigilant Aegis turns every Help into Protection from Evil and Good on the partner.

Pennon.split: Paragon 17 (Lionheart) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend, Pact of the Chain)
Pennon.note: Red Banner hands an ally a Reaction attack, and in a duo there is exactly one ally. Warlock 3 at characters 7-9 buys a second: Pact of the Chain's familiar is a permanent extra body that the banners can also target, and Agonizing Blast gives a heavy-armour Charisma body a ranged option it otherwise never has. Paragon 6 lands first so Banner Charges are on the short-rest clock before the dip, and Legendary Banner at 17 still gives the partner a free attack every turn for Charisma-mod turns. The cost is Beyond All Limits and the +4/+4.

Glasshand.note: Spellblade is a single-stat Charisma gish, and taking it mono ends in +4/+4. Mesmerist is the only other Charisma class in the list whose whole first three levels are single-stat too, so this dip costs nothing in spread and buys three things Paragon cannot reach: Hypnotic Stare, a permanent bonus-action penalty to one enemy's saves that spends no concentration and no resource; Towering Ego, Charisma added to Wisdom saves; and six short-rest Hypnotic Bonds carrying Mesmeric Mirror, which makes an attack on the partner automatically miss as a free action. Will Over Weave still lands at 13. The capstone does not.

Talonguard.note: Falling Rain doubles off Lone Wolf's second Action, and a third body doubles it again for less than the capstone costs. Ranger 1-3 at characters 6-8 lands a companion that already has Companion's Bond at level 3 under Expansion, a proficiency-scaled extra initiative slot that every Willpower Die spent still feeds around. The pair reads as three bodies from character 8 onward, which is what a Paragon's action economy actually lacks. Given up: Beyond All Limits, +4/+4, and the sixth Willpower Die.

Stormcalling.note: No dip at all, so Magical Secrets lands three times for six picks drawn from every list the modlist installs, and the 9th tier arrives — rather than six levels of Tempest maximising the damage types Stormcalling already deals and buying heavy armour on the way. Electrifying Aria at 14 is one Action that repeats a 12m Lightning burst for ten turns while degrading every caught enemy's Constitution save each turn, then Finale! converts the whole field into a mass Stun. It has no armour, no self-mitigation and nothing aimed at its own floor — the partner buys all of that.

Valour.note: Valour read as a way to make a Charisma caster's spells pay the partner rather than as a way to make one durable. Order 1, taken at characters 9-11, grants heavy armour on top of Valour's shields and Voice of Authority: every levelled spell this body casts on the other one hands them a free weapon attack. In a duo that is a spell list converted into the partner's action economy, and Battle Magic at 14 gives the caster a bonus-action swing on the same turn. Given up: Divine Smite, Lay on Hands, and half-caster slot progression.

Coda.split: Bard 17 (College of Swords) / Warlock 3 (The Fiend, Pact of the Blade)
Coda.note: Swords has Extra Attack at College level 6 and Flourishes already do what Battle Master dice would, so a martial dip is the one thing this College does not need. Warlock 3 at characters 9-11 buys what it does lack: second-level pact slots on the short-rest clock in a run where long rests cost 120 supplies, Agonizing Blast so a melee Bard has a Charisma-scaled answer at range, Repelling Blast as area control that spends no concentration, and Dark One's Blessing turning kills into temp HP. Master's Flourish at 14 keeps the Inspiration die for the partner.

Marginalia.split: Bard 17 (College of Lore) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One, Pact of the Chain)
Marginalia.note: A Lore Bard is worth keeping nearly whole, so this is the smallest possible departure. Bard runs to 10 first so both early Magical Secrets picks land untouched, then Warlock 1-3 at characters 11-13 fixes the two holes a pure Lore Bard keeps for twenty levels: it has no repeatable damage of its own, and its slots refuel only on the 120-supply rest. Agonizing Blast is a Charisma-scaled at-will floor, Pact of the Chain is a third body on the initiative order, and the pact slots come back twice a day for free. The bill is Magical Secrets at 18 and the 9th tier.

Psalter.split: Bard 14 (College of Lore) / Paladin 6 (Oath of Devotion)
Psalter.note: Six off-levels spent on Aura of Protection — Charisma added to every saving throw both bodies make, at Listo's 9m radius — rather than on a domain's heavy armour and outward temp-HP engine. Bard 1-3 first so the College and Expertise land in the prologue band, then Paladin 1-6 across characters 4-9. Divine Smite converts the Bard's own slot table into burst, and at Bard 14 plus half-caster 6 the table still reaches the 9th tier. Given up: heavy armour, Twilight Sanctuary, and six levels of Magical Secrets timing.

Masque.note: Glamour read as a tempo body that buys Actions rather than as a control body that buys the pair's floor. Fighter 1-3 at characters 7-9 lands Action Surge on a chassis whose best turns are cast-and-then-do-something-else, plus Manifest Echo, which is a second point in space to attack and teleport from and the closest thing a Bard gets to a body of its own. Mantle of Majesty is still a bonus-action Command that spends no concentration. The cost is the Peace domain's Emboldening Bond, so the saves on this body sit a full rung lower.

Stormthrow.note: A thrown-weapon Bard has two problems: tempo, and the fact that the body still stands in the middle of the fight to pick the weapon back up. This build buys for the second. Tempest 1-3 at characters 7-9 buys heavy armour and martial weapons, Wrath of the Storm as a reaction rider that Lone Wolf's second reaction fires twice a round, and Destructive Wrath to maximise the Thunder and Lightning the Bard is already casting. Given up: a second bonus action, and with it the throw-and-return loop's second iteration.

Dirge.split: Bard 17 (College of Tragedy) / Mesmerist 3 (Aspect of the Eyebiter)
Dirge.note: Three Mesmerist levels rather than the Sorcerer's Twinned and Quickened, because this is the one dip that compounds with Sorrowful Fate instead of running beside it. Tragedy converts any save the pair forces into a Charisma save; the Eyebiter's Bold Stare then hangs permanent Disadvantage on Charisma saves off a bonus-action Hypnotic Stare that costs no concentration and no resource, and the Stare's own minus-one rides on top. Every save the pair forces, from either body, is rolled at the enemy's worst stat with two penalties on it. It has no armour and no answer of its own to a crowd that reaches it.

Duskwyrm.split: Monk 17 (Way of the Ascendant Dragon) / Cleric 3 (Twilight Domain)
Duskwyrm.note: Three Cleric levels spent on rescue rather than on damage: Cleric 1-3 at characters 6-8 puts Twilight Sanctuary on a short-rest Channel Divinity while Act I is still being fought, and Aspect of the Wyrm at Monk 11 adds a second outward layer, since its Resistance option covers allies in the aura and not only the Monk. Nothing here maximises the dragon's Breath — Breath of the Dragon is unmaximised and stays on its own ki clock, so the AoE row is flat rather than spiked.

Lectern.split: Monk 17 (Way of the Friar) / Bard 3 (College of Lore)
Lectern.note: Friar stops paying out after Cleansing Wave, and three Bard levels fill that gap where six Cleric ones would not. Friar has Guidance always prepared, which is the half of the rung-3 skills clause no Monk in the list can buy; Lore at characters 6-8 supplies the other half and three bonus proficiencies with it, on a chassis that otherwise reads near zero out of combat. Staying to Monk 17 keeps the d12 Martial Arts die, and Pacifying Sweep at 6 is area control on a ki charge rather than a concentration slot. Given up: Emboldening Bond, heavy armour, and the Cleric slot table.

Quicksilver.split: Monk 17 (Way of the Four Elements) / Fighter 3 (Battle Master)
Quicksilver.note: One ki pool has to fund the disciplines, the Flurries and Stunning Strike at once, which is the problem this body solves from outside the Monk. Fighter 3 hands it a second short-rest pool: four superiority dice pay for the control riders ki was buying, Action Surge is a third Action that can cast a discipline without giving up the attack routine, and Second Wind is out-of-combat healing that keeps the long rest away. The Fighter tag opens the Hag's Hair on Intimidation DC 15 with advantage rather than Deception DC 20 — the route, not the roll: this body carries no Charisma and needs the bank or a partner to actually take it.

Cairnhand.split: Monk 17 (Way of the Astral Self) / Cleric 3 (Grave Domain)
Cairnhand.note: Three off-levels spent making the partner's turn bigger rather than making the Monk legible out of combat. Path to the Grave is a short-rest Channel Divinity that opens a vulnerability window on one creature, which in a duo is the partner's whole burst doubled on the priority target, and Grave's Circle of Mortality maximises any healing aimed at a body already at zero. Cleric is Wisdom-keyed, so the Monk's single-stat property survives intact. The cost is the entire skills axis: this body reads 1 out of combat for twenty levels.

Assize.split: Monk 17 (Way of the Open Hand) / Inquisitor 3 (Zeal Inquisition)
Assize.note: Stern Gaze is the cheap route to the social gates: it lets Intimidation run off Wisdom, which is the only non-Charisma answer to the Hag's Hair in the whole list and free on a body already at Wis 22. Inquisitor is Wisdom-keyed throughout, so Judgment's Resiliency and Destruction both run at full value on two short-rest charges, Righteous Vigilance stacks Wisdom onto initiative, and Monk stays the level-1 class so its own Strength and Dexterity saves survive. Open Hand's Topple and Push still ride every Flurry strike off the Ki Save DC.

Gorgon.split: Mesmerist 17 (Aspect of the Eyebiter) / Warlock 3 (The Great Old One, Pact of the Chain)
Gorgon.note: Mesmerist 20's immunity to all damage while Staring is the only line that a mono build buys, and everything below it already arrives at Mesmerist 10, where the Resistance boon covers all damage rather than only physical and proportional resistance stacked on Lone Wolf's halving is most of the value. So this body takes three levels elsewhere. Warlock supplies what an Eyebiter structurally lacks: Painful Stare fires once per turn on any damage to the Stare target, and Eldritch Blast with Agonizing Blast is the at-will Charisma-scaled delivery it never had, on short-rest slots, with a familiar to hold the third initiative slot.

Foible.note: This fixes the Panache problem at the source rather than routing around it with a Sneak Attack damage floor that does not care whether Panache is full. Panache comes back on a critical hit or a kill with a one-handed piercing weapon, so Improved Critical at Fighter 3 turns a rapier's crit range into the refill valve, Action Surge adds a whole Action of attack rolls to fish with, and Duelling pays two damage a hit for holding exactly the weapon the subclass demands. Extra Attack stays gated on three Panache, and now the gate holds. The cost is Rogue's Expertise, and with it two rungs of skills.

Redletter.split: Rogue 3 (Swashbuckler) / Blood Hunter 17 (Order of the Profane Soul)
Redletter.note: Six Wizard levels would pay for themselves in spread, since Intelligence keys everything here twice over — but they cost the class its whole back half and buy slots that only refill on a 120-supply rest. Rogue at character level 1 costs nothing at all in saves — Blood Hunter's own Intelligence and Dexterity pair is exactly what Rogue grants, so the duplication the class file warns about is avoided rather than paid — and it returns four proficiencies, Expertise twice, and a Sneak Attack that Swashbuckler makes at-will with no adjacent ally. Blood Hunter then runs to 17 with Sapping Scar, Tethering, Dark Augmentation and seven Blood Maledicts. The hole is AoE: pact slots stop at third level and the Warlock list has no Fireball, so this body brings none at all.

Quicksilver.verdict: One rest cadence funds both bodies. Ki, four superiority dice, Action Surge and Second Wind on the diving half; pact slots converted into Divine Smite on the other — nothing in this pairing waits on a long rest, and the short rest refills the burst on both sides at once. Six Paladin levels taken first are what make the dive survivable rather than reckless: heavy armour and Wisdom/Charisma saves from level 1, Extra Attack and Revivify at 5, and Aura of Protection at 6 adding the Charisma modifier to every saving throw both bodies make at 9m. Stunning Strike converts the Constitution saves the pair forces, Mortal Reminder fires off crits, and six damage types with none shared means no single resistance layer takes a meaningful share of the output.
Quicksilver.cost: Skills collapse and the number is not a soft one: rung 3 in Act I, 0 in Act II with utility at 0.0, and 1 in Act III. Neither body owns Expertise or a Rogue's proficiency spread, the Monk's Wisdom is spent on ki DCs and the Warlock-Paladin's Charisma on the aura and the smite, so past the opening act nothing here rolls against Act II's dialogue and detection band. The Fighter tag opens Hag's Hair on Intimidation DC 15 with advantage, but the route is all it opens — the roll still has to come from a body that carries the modifier. The aura is also a 9m leash on a Four Elements Monk whose whole routine is leaving it, and taking the oath block first surrenders Mystic Arcanum 8th and 9th and pushes the Entropic Ward line late.

vars.note: An armoured Bard with a die it can spend on the Monk's armour class, which buys the outward layer without the 9m leash.
Full Expertise and three rounds of Magical Secrets, so the skills axis stops reading zero — and the armour and the revive go with it.
A ranged Stare that mills a boss while the Monk works the crowd, and neither body gains a point of durability.

Gorgon.verdict: Painful Stare fires once per turn on any damage reaching the Stare target, and a d12 Martial Arts die landing a flurry into that creature guarantees the trigger on a turn the Eyebiter spends doing something else — so the Stare mills whether or not the ranged body attacks. Out of combat the two halves are a face and a scout rather than two of either: the Warlock dip carries Charisma delivery on short-rest slots, the Friar has Guidance always prepared, and Lore at characters 6–8 adds Expertise and three bonus proficiencies. That is what holds the pair at rung 3 in Act III, where the field's ceiling is 3 and most duos are below it. Proportional Resistance at Mesmerist 10 covers all damage rather than only physical and stacks on Lone Wolf's own halving, so the resilience comes from the boon rather than from armour neither body wears.
Gorgon.cost: Act I is bought and paid for elsewhere: tempo 0.388, action economy at 3, area control at 2, and duration at 2, because the Warlock levels and the Lore dip both land in the character 6–9 band and neither engine is finished before Act II. The crowd flag sits on the melee half, so every fight against numbers is fought a body down — and the Stare's whole reward structure is holding one creature, which is exactly the wrong instinct against a room. Area damage, area control and duration are all holes; Pacifying Sweep on a ki charge is the entire answer. There is no heavy armour, no Cleric slot table and no revive anywhere in the pairing.

vars.note: Heavy armour and a real front rank, bought by giving up Expertise and always-prepared Guidance.
An Intelligence caster with two slot tables and a save rider, which is coverage this pairing has no route to.
A second short-rest burst engine in melee, and the skills rung goes down with the Lore dip.

Dawnblind.verdict: The blind is the setup and the crit range is the payoff, and neither half is worth much without the other. Radiance of the Dawn is a short-rest area radiant burst that spares allies, so every creature it touches rolls Glaring Frost's Constitution save or is Blinded, and Snowborn Anthelion at 15 spreads that save three metres from each of them. Attacks against a blinded creature have advantage, and the Paladin is the body built to cash that in: Improved Critical's 19-20 under advantage crits close to a fifth of all swings, Action Surge is a third Action on a body that already has two, and every crit doubles both Divine Smite's dice and Fount of Moonlight's +2d6 radiant. Snow Blindness charges the same crowd for every action it takes in the meantime, and Remarkable Athlete's +3 initiative gets the burst out first.
Dawnblind.cost: The two halves cast off different stats — the blind DC is Wisdom and the aura and the smites are Charisma — so no single item lifts both sides, and against anything that cannot be blinded the crit math is just a Paladin swinging. Skills are the holed axis: 4 in Act I, 3 in Act II, 2 by Act III, with no third body to cover the traps and doors neither of these two is built to read. Radiant is on both sheets, so the resistance that taxes one half taxes the other at the same time. And the Paladin bought the swing by giving up Twilight Sanctuary's every-round temp HP, which leaves nothing in the pairing that sustains a long fight and no outward healing anywhere in it.

vars.note: A Charisma face and a pact-slot damage floor on short-rest slots, bought by giving up the aura and the heavy armour under it.
Buys an outward blessing and a revive, on a body with far less to do with a blinded room.
Two short-rest area engines pointed at the same crowd, with nobody left carrying the run's checks.

Moonsong.name: Moonsong & Lectern
Moonsong.verdict: Reads as. The anchor arrangement: a heavy-armoured static aura body in front and an unarmoured skirmisher working around it, which is what makes the Monk's missing armour stop mattering. Both halves took the same Lore dip, so both carry Cutting Words — with Lone Wolf's extra reaction that is a denial the pair can spend on nearly every enemy roll that matters, landing on the same roll the aura is already subtracting from.
Moonsong.cost: Costs. The capstone is surrendered outright, and it was the party-wide save bonus and the extra reaction — the two things an aura build most wants. Neither body is a damage engine, so the pair kills slowly against the run's inflated health, and the static half cannot follow the mobile one out of the aura it is the whole point of.

vars.text: The mono reading: Moonward keeps the capstone and reads near nothing out of combat for the entire run. This spends the top of the oath on the half of the game the aura never touched, and every aura feature that matters is already in place long before the trade is made.
Charisma stays clean: nothing in the Lore dip asks for a second stat, so the split costs a paladin nothing in the only currency it actually spends.

Wyrmwarden.name: Wyrmwarden & Lectern
Wyrmwarden.verdict: Reads as. Twilight Sanctuary is a no-action aura that puts temporary hit points on the partner every round off a charge the short rest refunds, and the partner is an unarmoured Monk — the body on the board with most to gain from a standing outward layer that costs it no turn. Elemental Affinity still writes Charisma onto every dart, so the ranged half keeps its damage while the melee half stops being made of paper, and between them the pair covers four damage types with nothing doubled.
Wyrmwarden.cost: Costs. The whole outward answer sits on one body: when the Sorcerer is the one on the floor, the Monk has nothing to pick it up with, and temporary hit points were never healing to begin with. Skills fall away entirely by the last act, so the run's late gates go unanswered, and nothing in the pairing reaches a crowd at the rung the model asks for — the domain's heavy armour, meanwhile, cannot be worn by the half that actually needs it.

vars.note: An armoured static body that holds ground and crits into smites, in place of the skirmisher carrying the pair's skills.

vars.text: Against the mono reading: the pure bloodline never reached the other character in any act. This is the smallest dip that changes that, and it changes it while the first act is still being fought.
Concentration: the sanctuary needs none of it, which leaves the whole concentration budget free for the things a Monk cannot supply.

Coda.verdict: The partner's whole routine is bonus actions and thrown objects, which is exactly what a melee Bard in light armour has no way to buy. Fast Hands on top of Lone Wolf's second bonus action is three conjure-and-throw bonus actions a round: grease bottles and caustic bulbs lay persistent surfaces that spend no slot and no concentration, Repelling Blast pushes things onto them for free, and thrown healing potions reach a front-rank body that owns no healing of its own. Both halves refuel without a long rest in a run that prices one at 120 supplies — pact slots on the short-rest clock against an item engine that is rest-free outright — and between them the damage types run acid, fire, force and slashing with nothing repeated. Dark One's Blessing turns the kills the surfaces set up into temp HP, and Master's Flourish at 14 keeps sending the Inspiration die across.
Coda.cost: Durability is the hole and both bodies own it: a melee Bard in light armour beside a Wizard, sharing a rank that nothing anchors, with resilience reading 0.57 in Act I and never clearing 0.61. The potions answer damage after it has landed, not before. And the item engine is the wrong shape against a single high-value target — bombs and vials are built for numbers — so priority fights are the ones this pair takes a body down, which is also where the throw-and-surface control has the least to grip. Neither half sustains: nothing on either sheet lasts past the turn it was spent on.

vars.note: Two outward mitigation layers pointed at the Bard, bought by giving up the item engine and the ranged half with it.
Guidance always prepared and a second Expertise set, and a second unarmoured body standing in the same rank.
Twinned wards over both bodies at once, on a partner with even less armour than this one.

Wyrmcall.verdict: Reaction riders are the join. Lunar Champion at 20 hands out a third Reaction on top of Lone Wolf's second, and Tempest 3 brings Wrath of the Storm — a rider that fires on being hit — onto a Monk that dives into the middle of everything, so the extra Reactions land on the one body positioned to be hit repeatedly and every incoming swing pays lightning back out. The rest is a clean division: Draconic Strike is a toggle, so the whole subclass is set to lightning and Destructive Wrath maximises a Breath of the Dragon that already costs no bonus action, while the other half is prevention only — Aura of Moonlight's flat minus-Charisma on every hit either body takes, Divine Guardian halving all damage on the partner off a short-rest charge, and the capstone's Charisma-modifier bonus to every saving throw both bodies make. Aspect of the Wyrm at character 14 is the only Monk feature in the list that buffs the partner back.
Wyrmcall.cost: Skills are where this pairing genuinely fails rather than merely thins: 3 in Act I, then 0 in Act II and 1 in Act III. Neither body buys Expertise or a Perception proficiency, and against Act II's bands the pair's mean clear rate across the act's checks falls under a quarter — that is not a soft landing, it is no out-of-combat coverage at all for most of the run. In the fight, the aura has a radius and the Monk keeps leaving it, so the mitigation the pairing is built on lapses exactly on the turns the Monk commits. The tempo half is one damage type end to end, and the layered resistances late in the run are aimed at precisely that. Nothing here clears a crowd except the Breath, which sits on its own pool.

vars.note: Trades the standing aura for one that follows the Monk in, and buys the pair a real skill floor with it.
Doubles down on the damage type instead of covering the Monk, and hands the pairing a second body that maximises the same burst.

vars.text: Why the domain dip and not more Monk: the maximising Channel Divinity is the only thing in the list that makes an already-free Breath worth building the subclass toggle around, and it lands on the stat the Ki save DC already runs on.

Aria.name: Aria & Moonward
Aria.verdict: Reads as. Electrifying Aria degrades every caught enemy's Constitution save each turn it persists and ends by converting the field into a mass stun — and Moonward is the partner that can stand inside it and take the return fire, subtracting a flat amount from every hit either body eats and halving what lands on the Bard off a short-rest charge. Tempest also puts heavy armour on a Charisma caster, so the ranged half is not paying for its position in hit points.
Aria.cost: Costs. The wide answer never reaches the rung the model wants, because all of it is one concentration aura: break it and the crowd clear, the save degradation and the stun it was building toward vanish together. The Paladin is not a damage body and never becomes one, so tempo rests on a blaster dealing two types the endgame is built to resist, and every outward layer in the pairing belongs to the half that is not casting.

vars.note: A Monk converting the failed Constitution saves the aura manufactures, at the price of the armour holding the line.
A blessing and a revive in place of the prevention, and the pair's concentration is spoken for twice over.

Immolate.name: Immolate & Lectern
Immolate.verdict: Reads as. Nothing on the lead holds concentration, which is rare on a Wisdom caster and is the whole argument: the pair never chooses between a standing effect and its own burst, and the budget belongs to whatever else it wants running. Underneath sits a full martial routine with an extra Action on top and a maximised elemental burst off charges the short rest returns, beside a Monk covering the same Constitution saves on a ki clock.
Immolate.cost: Costs. Nothing in the pairing controls a crowd — the sweep is the only wide answer and it is a single ki charge, so a room arrives all at once and gets answered one body at a time. Skills also collapse to nothing by the last act, and both halves are melee, so anything on a ledge or in the air is dealt with by walking to it.

vars.note: Real control opposite the weapon routine, on a body the enemy AI picks before either of these.
A ranged Stare that mills a boss down, which is the answer this pairing cannot reach with its feet.
Twinned wards and a slot-free area lockdown, at the price of every point of armour on that side.

Duskwyrm.tag: twilight dragon monk + twinning archfey warlock
Duskwyrm.verdict: Every outward layer in this pairing lands on both bodies, which is rarer than it sounds — most rescue stacks protect the body carrying them. Twilight Sanctuary arrives on a short-rest Channel Divinity while Act I is still being fought, temp-HPing anything standing in it for no action, and Aspect of the Wyrm at Monk 11 adds a second aura whose Resistance option covers the ally rather than only its carrier. Against that, a two-person party is a party Twinned Spell covers entirely: Twinned Death Ward from character 10 is prevention on both halves out of one cast, Twinned Greater Invisibility is both halves untargetable, and Quickened is the only reliable route to a third cast in a turn under Listo's bonus-action-spell rule. The rescue row reads 5, 6, 6 and it is reciprocal — the ward is already on the Monk before the Monk is the one on the floor. Both sides also run entirely off the short rest, ki and Channel Divinity against pact slots that Font of Magic converts into sorcery points and back, which is the most rest-independent shape available in a run that charges three supplies a camp.
Duskwyrm.cost: Durability is the hole and it never moves: 2 in every act, because the row takes the worse of the two bodies and neither has armour worth the name — an unarmoured Monk beside a Warlock whose entire answer is Draconic Resilience and light armour. Temporary hit points and resistance are not the same thing as not being hit, and all of it is a refund after the fact. Skills are the second hole and they stop after the opening act: 3 in Act I, 0 in Act II with utility at 0.0, 1 in Act III. Neither body owns Expertise or a wide proficiency spread, and the Wisdom and Intelligence that read traps, caches and secret doors are spent elsewhere on both sheets — ki DCs on one, the pact on the other. The area row is also flat rather than spiked, because nothing here maximises the dragon's Breath: Breath of the Dragon stays unmaximised on its own ki clock, and Fey Presence controls a crowd without damaging it, so the pairing never has a round that simply clears the room.

vars.note: Keeps the shared casting stat and adds a blind engine, so the sanctuary is protecting bodies nothing can see.
Heavy armour and an outward blessing on it — a body that can hold ground, rather than another ward layered on one that cannot.
Two Monks splitting one job on the same Wisdom DC, and the pair's Charisma coverage leaves with the Warlock.

Brimstone.verdict: The ki pool stops being asked to do everything. Way of the Four Elements has one pool funding the disciplines, the Flurries and Stunning Strike at once, and the Fiend takes the whole wide half of the job off it: the only patron whose expanded list is a genuine burst under Eldritch Cone — Fireball, Wall of Fire, Flame Strike — with Consuming Fervor maximising it on a Channel Divinity charge the short rest refunds. Ki is left to pay for stuns and extra strikes and nothing else. The Zeal dip is also what puts a light-armour caster in heavy armour, a shield and martial weapons at level 1 while keeping the Wisdom and Charisma save pair, so the unarmoured body is not the only one holding a front rank. Fighter 3 answers the same problem from the other side: four superiority dice buy the control riders ki was buying, Action Surge is a third Action that casts a discipline without giving up the attack routine, and Second Wind is healing that keeps the long rest away. Every resource on both sheets comes back on the same short rest.
Brimstone.cost: Nothing here is aimed at the other body. Rescue reads 2, 2, 1 across the three acts and the number is honest: Second Wind heals its own carrier, Fiendish Resilience protects its own carrier and is re-picked at every rest — a guess about the next fight rather than an answer to this one — and there is no revival, no condition removal and no outward heal anywhere in the pairing, so a Held or downed half is half the party gone until the fight ends. Skills are the second hole and they fail in the middle rather than at the end: 3 in Act I, 0 in Act II with utility at 0.0, 1 in Act III. Neither body owns Expertise or a wide proficiency spread, and the Wisdom and Intelligence that read traps, caches and secret doors are dump stats on both sheets, so from the Shadowlands on the pair walks into whatever it did not spot. The damage spread is four types wide and the whole burst half is fire, which is exactly what the endgame's layered resistances punish hardest.

vars.note: A melee Charisma body that carries its own pact floor, so the front rank stops being the Monk's job alone.
An every-round temp-HP aura aimed outward and a Rogue's full proficiency spread, which are the two rows this pairing reads nothing on.
An armoured Bard with a die it can hand over for armour class, in place of the pairing's whole skill budget.

Tidesong.verdict: Wrath of the Sea is concentration and wants to run every fight, and the partner spent six levels buying the thing that keeps it up: Aura of Protection, Charisma added to every saving throw both bodies make, at Listo's 9m radius. Concentration checks are Constitution saves, so the aura is not a general nicety here — it is the reason the pairing's core engine survives being hit, and saves read 5 in all three acts because of it. The rest compounds from the same purchase: Divine Smite converts a Bard slot table into burst, and at Bard 14 with half-caster 6 that table still reaches the 9th tier, while the lead keeps the full caster progression, the summons and the ritual list intact. Both halves bought Expertise from opposite directions, which is how a Druid pairing clears a skill floor no Druid in the roster clears alone.
Tidesong.cost: Durability is the holed axis and neither body fixes it — the aura buys a save bonus, not a damage reduction, and the partner gave up heavy armour and an outward temp-HP engine to afford it. The concentration budget is spoken for before anything else is cast, which is why control never gets above 4 or 5 and drops again in Act III. Both bodies also want their bonus action every single turn and only one gets it uncontested. Two Bard-carrying sheets means the skill split is less disjoint than the Expertise count suggests: 4 through the first two acts, 3 in the third. Tempo falls back to 0.586 in Act III as the area half thins out.

vars.text: The Tempest reading: the same Circle with a domain dip keeps maximised thunder and an outward heal, and reads at the roster's Druid floor on skills for the whole run. This trades the burst for the half of the game the Druid list never covered.
Making the weapon half real: a Fighting Style, scimitar proficiency and Blade Flourishes matter here precisely because the bonus action is already committed elsewhere every turn.

Nightbloom.tag: twilight moon paladin + snowlight blind ranger
Nightbloom.verdict: Blind the room, then stand in it. Radiance of the Dawn spares allies, so the armoured half takes no part of the burst that makes every creature around it roll Glaring Frost's Constitution save, and Snowborn Anthelion at Ranger 15 carries that save three metres further. What comes back the other way is the reason the fragile half survives being that close: Twilight Sanctuary is a no-action aura that hands the Ranger temp HP every single round, it recharges twice per short rest at Cleric 6, and Cleric 7 adds Death Ward on top. The whole pairing runs one clock — sanctuary, Radiance and Snow Blindness's tax on every action a blinded enemy takes all come back on the break, and blinded attackers swinging at disadvantage into standing temp HP is the loop.
Nightbloom.cost: Action economy reads 3 in every act and nothing raises it — no Action Surge, no third bonus action, no extra body — so this pairing wins by outlasting rather than by acting, in a run that charges supplies for the rest the outlasting depends on. Both halves also carry Cleric levels, and a shared class is precisely what the Skills axis punishes: rung 4 in Act I falls to 2 by Act III with utility at 0.38, because two Wisdom dips buy the same short-rest area effect twice instead of buying a second kind of coverage. The lead surrenders Lunar Champion, Silvered Rebuke and four levels of slots, and splits its casting across two stats so neither DC is as high as a single-stat body's. Both halves deal radiant, so one resistance layer takes the damage and the control together.

vars.text: Against the capstone reading: Moonward keeps the whole oath and draws its prevention from a long-rest clock and a level-twenty line. This gets most of the same prevention off a charge the short rest returns, which is the clock the rest of the pairing already runs on.
Auras do not stack: partner this with another aura body and the second one is decoration, which quietly rules out a whole column of the field.

vars.note: Expertise and always-prepared Guidance in place of the blind engine, and the skills fall stops — along with the second radiant source.

Cloister.name: Cloister & Aria
Cloister.verdict: Reads as.
